ko.title: [Logistics 101 #9] 운동화는 태평양을 건너는 데 동전 몇 푼이면 충분했다 — 그런데 마지막 3마일이 더 비싸다

segments.src: > Moving freight 8,000 miles is a solved, cheap, standardized problem; moving it the final 3 miles to your porch is the expensive, unsolved one — and the math behind those last 3 miles is genuinely hard.
segments.tr: > 화물을 8,000마일 옮기는 것은 이미 해결된, 저렴하고 표준화된 문제입니다. 그 화물을 마지막 3마일, 즉 현관까지 옮기는 것이 비싸고 아직 풀리지 않은 문제이며, 그 마지막 3마일 뒤의 수학은 정말 어렵습니다.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 오늘의 개념

segments.src: Three ideas do most of the work in modern transportation management.
segments.tr: 현대 운송 관리의 대부분은 세 가지 개념이 담당합니다.

segments.src: Intermodal and multimodal transport.** A shipment rarely uses one mode.
segments.tr: 인터모달 운송과 멀티모달 운송.** 화물은 하나의 운송수단만 쓰는 경우가 드뭅니다.

segments.src: It rides a ship, then a truck, then a train, then another truck.
segments.tr: 배에 실렸다가, 트럭으로, 다시 기차로, 또 다른 트럭으로 이동합니다.

segments.src: The trick that makes this cheap is the **shipping container**: a standardized steel box that gets lifted between modes without anyone touching the goods inside.
segments.tr: 이를 저렴하게 만드는 핵심은 **화물 컨테이너**입니다. 운송수단이 바뀔 때마다 안의 화물을 건드리지 않고 들어 올릴 수 있도록 규격화된 강철 상자입니다.

segments.src: Load it once in a factory in Vietnam, unload it once at a warehouse in Ohio.
segments.tr: 베트남 공장에서 한 번 싣고, 오하이오 창고에서 한 번 내립니다.

segments.src: The two words are often used interchangeably, but there's a useful distinction in contracts.
segments.tr: 두 용어는 종종 혼용되지만, 계약서에서는 유용한 구분이 있습니다.

segments.src: *Intermodal* usually describes the physical fact — several modes, one loading unit, often several separate carrier contracts.
segments.tr: *인터모달*은 보통 물리적 사실을 가리킵니다 — 여러 운송수단이 하나의 적재 단위를 사용하며, 종종 별도의 운송사 계약이 여러 개 있습니다.

segments.src: *Multimodal* usually describes the commercial fact — **one contract, one operator liable for the whole door-to-door journey**, typically under a single through bill of lading.
segments.tr: *멀티모달*은 보통 상업적 사실을 가리킵니다 — **하나의 계약, 문 앞에서 문 앞까지 전 구간에 책임지는 하나의 사업자**이며, 대개 단일 통합 선하증권 아래 이루어집니다.

segments.src: That matters when something goes wrong.
segments.tr: 이는 문제가 생겼을 때 중요합니다.

segments.src: Under separate contracts, you have to prove *which* leg damaged the cargo.
segments.tr: 계약이 구간별로 나뉘어 있으면, 화물이 *어느 구간에서* 손상되었는지 입증해야 합니다.

segments.src: Under a single multimodal contract, you have one party to call.
segments.tr: 단일 멀티모달 계약 아래에서는 연락할 상대가 한 곳입니다.

segments.src: The last mile.** The final leg from a local depot to the customer's door.
segments.tr: **라스트 마일.** 현지 물류거점에서 고객의 문 앞까지의 마지막 구간입니다.

segments.src: It's the leg where economies of scale collapse.
segments.tr: 이 구간은 규모의 경제가 무너지는 곳입니다.

segments.src: A truck leaving the Port of Long Beach carries one container to one place.
segments.tr: 롱비치 항을 떠난 트럭은 컨테이너 하나를 한 곳으로 실어 갑니다.

segments.src: A delivery van carries 120 separate packages to 120 separate addresses, each with its own driveway, elevator, gate code, and dog.
segments.tr: 배송 밴은 120개의 개별 소포를 120개의 서로 다른 주소로 싣고 갑니다. 주소마다 진입로, 엘리베이터, 출입 비밀번호, 그리고 개가 있습니다.

segments.src: Industry studies commonly put last-mile delivery at roughly 40–50% of total parcel logistics cost — the shortest leg, the biggest bill.
segments.tr: 업계 연구에서는 보통 라스트 마일 배송이 전체 택배 물류비의 약 40–50%를 차지한다고 봅니다 — 가장 짧은 구간이 가장 큰 청구서입니다.

segments.src: Two levers dominate last-mile economics:
segments.tr: 라스트 마일의 경제성은 두 가지 요인이 좌우합니다:

segments.src: - **Stop density** — how many deliveries you make per mile driven. Dense city blocks are cheap per package; rural routes are brutal.
segments.tr: - **정차 밀도** — 차량이 1마일 주행할 때 몇 건을 배송하는가. 도심 블록은 소포당 비용이 낮고, 농촌 노선은 가혹합니다.

segments.src: - **First-attempt success rate** — a failed delivery roughly doubles the cost of that package. This is why lockers, pickup points (PUDO), and "leave at door" photos exist. They're not conveniences; they're cost controls.
segments.tr: - **첫 시도 성공률** — 배송 실패 한 번은 해당 소포의 비용을 대략 두 배로 만듭니다. 그래서 무인 보관함, 픽업 포인트(PUDO), "문 앞에 두기" 사진이 존재합니다. 편의 기능이 아니라 비용 통제 수단입니다.

segments.src: The Vehicle Routing Problem (VRP).** Once you have 120 packages and 8 vans, someone has to decide who delivers what, in what order.
segments.tr: **차량 경로 문제(VRP).** 소포 120개와 밴 8대가 있으면, 누가 무엇을 어떤 순서로 배송할지 결정해야 합니다.

segments.src: That's the VRP, formally introduced by Dantzig and Ramser in 1959.
segments.tr: 이것이 VRP이며, 1959년 Dantzig와 Ramser가 공식적으로 제시했습니다.

segments.src: Its simpler cousin is the **Traveling Salesman Problem**: one vehicle, visit every stop once, return home, minimize distance.
segments.tr: 더 단순한 사촌 문제는 **외판원 문제(TSP)**입니다: 차량 한 대가 모든 정차지를 한 번씩 방문하고, 출발지로 돌아와, 거리를 최소화합니다.

segments.src: TSP is just a VRP with a single uncapacitated vehicle.
segments.tr: TSP는 용량 제한이 없는 차량 한 대짜리 VRP일 뿐입니다.

segments.src: Why is this hard?
segments.tr: 왜 어려울까요?

segments.src: Because the number of possible sequences explodes:
segments.tr: 가능한 순서의 수가 폭발적으로 늘어나기 때문입니다:

segments.src: 20 stops  ->  20! orderings  ->  about 2,400,000,000,000,000,000 (2.4 quintillion)
segments.tr: 20 stops  ->  20! orderings  ->  about 2,400,000,000,000,000,000 (2.4 quintillion)

segments.src: Checking them all is hopeless, and VRP is **NP-hard** — no known algorithm finds the guaranteed-best answer quickly as the problem grows.
segments.tr: 모두 검사하는 것은 불가능하며, VRP는 **NP-난해(NP-hard)**입니다 — 문제가 커질수록 보장된 최적해를 빠르게 찾는 알려진 알고리즘이 없습니다.

segments.src: Real routing software doesn't look for the perfect route.
segments.tr: 실제 경로 계획 소프트웨어는 완벽한 경로를 찾으려 하지 않습니다.

segments.src: It uses **heuristics**: rules that find a very good route fast.
segments.tr: 대신 **휴리스틱**, 즉 매우 좋은 경로를 빠르게 찾아내는 규칙을 사용합니다.

segments.src: The classic is the Clarke–Wright savings algorithm (1964), which asks how much you save by combining two separate out-and-back trips into one:
segments.tr: 고전적인 방법은 Clarke–Wright 절약 알고리즘(1964)으로, 두 개의 개별 왕복 운행을 하나로 합치면 얼마나 절약되는지를 묻습니다:

segments.src: savings(i, j) = dist(depot, i) + dist(depot, j) - dist(i, j)
segments.tr: savings(i, j) = dist(depot, i) + dist(depot, j) - dist(i, j)

segments.src: Merge the pairs with the biggest savings first, stop when the truck is full.
segments.tr: 절약 효과가 가장 큰 쌍부터 합치고, 차량이 가득 차면 멈춥니다.

segments.src: Modern solvers layer on constraints that make it realistic: vehicle capacity, driver hours, and **time windows** — "deliver between 2 and 5 p.m."
segments.tr: 최신 솔버는 현실성을 높이는 제약을 추가합니다: 차량 용량, 기사 근무시간, 그리고 **시간창** — "오후 2시에서 5시 사이 배송" 같은 조건입니다.

segments.src: That variant is VRPTW, and every time window you add shrinks the space of legal routes and raises the cost.
segments.tr: 이 변형이 VRPTW이며, 시간창을 하나 추가할 때마다 허용되는 경로의 범위가 줄어들고 비용이 올라갑니다.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 일상 속에서

segments.src: You order a $70 pair of running shoes on a Tuesday night.
segments.tr: 화요일 밤에 70달러짜리 러닝화 한 켤레를 주문합니다.

segments.src: Here's the actual chain:
segments.tr: 실제 과정은 다음과 같습니다:

segments.src: The shoes were containerized in Vietnam.
segments.tr: 이 운동화는 베트남에서 컨테이너에 실렸습니다.

segments.src: A 40-foot container holds several thousand pairs, so at a few thousand dollars for the ocean leg, the trans-Pacific voyage costs well under **$1 per pair** (figures are illustrative and move constantly with market rates).
segments.tr: 40피트 컨테이너에는 수천 켤레가 들어가므로, 해상 구간 비용이 수천 달러라 해도 태평양 횡단 운송은 켤레당 **1달러 미만**입니다(수치는 예시이며 시장 운임에 따라 계속 변합니다).

segments.src: The box lands at the Port of Los Angeles/Long Beach.
segments.tr: 컨테이너는 로스앤젤레스/롱비치 항에 도착합니다.

segments.src: A short-haul **drayage** truck hauls it a few miles to a rail ramp — a leg of maybe 20 miles that can cost a few hundred dollars for the container.
segments.tr: 단거리 **드레이지(항만 단거리 운송)** 트럭이 이를 몇 마일 떨어진 철도 상차장까지 나릅니다. 약 20마일 구간이며 컨테이너 한 개당 수백 달러가 들 수 있습니다.

segments.src: Then a BNSF or Union Pacific intermodal train carries it to the Chicago area, the country's biggest inland rail hub, where a truck takes it to a regional distribution center.
segments.tr: 그다음 BNSF나 Union Pacific의 인터모달 열차가 미국 최대의 내륙 철도 거점인 시카고 지역까지 실어 나르고, 트럭이 이를 지역 물류센터로 옮깁니다.

segments.src: Everything so far was cheap per pair, because everything so far moved *thousands of pairs at once*.
segments.tr: 여기까지는 모든 구간이 *수천 켤레를 한꺼번에* 움직였기 때문에 켤레당 비용이 저렴했습니다.

segments.src: Then you click "buy."
segments.tr: 그리고 "구매"를 클릭합니다.

segments.src: Now one pair, in one box, needs to reach one address.
segments.tr: 이제 한 상자 안의 한 켤레를 한 주소로 보내야 합니다.

segments.src: It gets picked, sorted, trucked to a local delivery station, and loaded onto a van with ~120 other packages.
segments.tr: 상품은 피킹되고 분류되어 지역 배송 거점으로 옮겨진 뒤, 다른 약 120개 소포와 함께 밴에 실립니다.

segments.src: That van's driver burns fuel, time, and wages for **your** stop specifically — and the retailer's cost for that final leg is typically several dollars, more than the ocean, rail, and highway legs combined.
segments.tr: 그 밴의 기사는 **고객님의** 정차지를 위해 연료, 시간, 임금을 씁니다. 소매업체가 이 마지막 구간에 치르는 비용은 보통 몇 달러로, 항만·철도·고속도로 구간을 합친 것보다 많습니다.

segments.src: This is also why UPS famously routes its drivers to avoid left turns where practical.
segments.tr: 그래서 UPS는 가능한 경우 좌회전을 피하도록 기사들의 경로를 짜는 것으로 유명합니다.

segments.src: Waiting to cross oncoming traffic burns fuel and time and raises collision risk.
segments.tr: 맞은편 차량을 기다리며 좌회전하면 연료와 시간이 낭비되고 충돌 위험도 커집니다.

segments.src: UPS's ORION routing system, rolled out across its U.S.
segments.tr: UPS의 ORION 경로 시스템은 2016년까지 미국 전역 네트워크에 도입되었으며,

segments.src: network by 2016, applies that logic at scale; the company has said it saves roughly 100 million miles and about 10 million gallons of fuel a year.
segments.tr: 이 논리를 대규모로 적용합니다. 회사는 연간 약 1억 마일과 약 1천만 갤런의 연료를 절약한다고 밝혔습니다.

segments.src: That's a company figure, not an independent audit — but the direction is real.
segments.tr: 이는 회사가 발표한 수치이며 독립적인 감사 결과가 아닙니다 — 그러나 방향성은 실재합니다.

segments.src: When you're solving a VRP 55,000 times a day, a small per-stop improvement compounds into a very large number.
segments.tr: 하루에 55,000번 VRP를 푼다면, 정차당 작은 개선이 매우 큰 수치로 누적됩니다.

segments.src: ## The 3-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## 3줄 요약

segments.src: 1. Intermodal/multimodal transport makes long-haul freight absurdly cheap by standardizing the box and never touching the goods — and a single multimodal contract means one party is liable end to end.
segments.tr: 1. 인터모달/멀티모달 운송은 컨테이너를 표준화하고 화물을 절대 건드리지 않음으로써 장거리 화물 운송을 놀라울 만큼 저렴하게 만들며, 단일 멀티모달 계약은 한 사업자가 처음부터 끝까지 책임진다는 뜻입니다.

segments.src: 2. The last mile is the shortest and most expensive leg, roughly 40–50% of parcel cost, and it lives or dies on stop density and first-attempt success.
segments.tr: 2. 라스트 마일은 가장 짧으면서도 가장 비싼 구간으로, 택배 비용의 약 40–50%를 차지하며, 정차 밀도와 첫 시도 성공률에 따라 성패가 갈립니다.

segments.src: 3. Routing that last mile is the Vehicle Routing Problem — NP-hard, so real systems use heuristics for a very good answer rather than searching forever for a perfect one.
segments.tr: 3. 라스트 마일의 경로 계획은 차량 경로 문제입니다 — NP-난해하므로, 실제 시스템은 완벽한 답을 무한정 찾는 대신 휴리스틱으로 매우 좋은 답을 구합니다.

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ 자기 점검 퀴즈

segments.src: **Q1.** For a pair of shoes shipped from Asia to a U.S.
segments.tr: **Q1.** 아시아에서 미국 가정으로 배송되는 신발 한 켤레의 경우,

segments.src: home, which leg typically costs the *most* per unit delivered?
segments.tr: 배송 단위당 비용이 보통 *가장 많이* 드는 구간은 어디입니까?

segments.src: - (A) The trans-Pacific ocean voyage
segments.tr: - (A) 태평양 횡단 해상 운송

segments.src: - (B) The intermodal rail move to Chicago
segments.tr: - (B) 시카고까지의 인터모달 철도 이동

segments.src: - (C) The final van delivery to your door
segments.tr: - (C) 집 문 앞까지의 최종 밴 배송

segments.src: - (D) The drayage move out of the port
segments.tr: - (D) 항만에서 나오는 드레이지 이동

segments.src: **Q2.** O/X: The Traveling Salesman Problem can be described as a special case of the Vehicle Routing Problem.
segments.tr: **Q2.** O/X: 외판원 문제(TSP)는 차량 경로 문제(VRP)의 특수한 경우로 설명할 수 있다.

segments.src: **Q3.** Which change turns a standard VRP into a "VRPTW"?
segments.tr: **Q3.** 표준 VRP를 "VRPTW"로 바꾸는 변경은 무엇입니까?

segments.src: - (A) Adding vehicle capacity limits
segments.tr: - (A) 차량 용량 제한 추가

segments.src: - (B) Adding customer time windows
segments.tr: - (B) 고객 시간창 추가

segments.src: - (C) Allowing multiple depots
segments.tr: - (C) 여러 물류거점 허용

segments.src: - (D) Requiring the vehicle to return empty
segments.tr: - (D) 차량이 빈 채로 복귀하도록 요구

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 오늘의 용어

segments.src: - **Intermodal transport** — Moving goods by two or more modes in the same loading unit (usually a container), without handling the goods themselves at transfer points.
segments.tr: - **인터모달 운송** — 같은 적재 단위(보통 컨테이너)에 담긴 채로 둘 이상의 운송수단으로 화물을 옮기며, 환적 지점에서 화물 자체를 다루지 않는 방식.

segments.src: - **Multimodal transport** — The commercial version: one contract and one operator responsible for the entire door-to-door journey, typically under a through bill of lading.
segments.tr: - **멀티모달 운송** — 상업적 개념: 문 앞에서 문 앞까지 전 구간을 하나의 계약과 하나의 사업자가 책임지며, 보통 통합 선하증권 아래 이루어집니다.

segments.src: - **Drayage** — Short-distance trucking of a container, usually between a port, rail ramp, or nearby warehouse.
segments.tr: - **드레이지** — 컨테이너의 단거리 육상 운송으로, 보통 항만, 철도 상차장, 인근 창고 사이에서 이루어집니다.

segments.src: - **Stop density** — Deliveries made per mile driven; the single biggest driver of last-mile cost per package.
segments.tr: - **정차 밀도** — 1마일 주행당 배송 건수로, 소포당 라스트 마일 비용을 가장 크게 좌우하는 요인입니다.

segments.src: - **Vehicle Routing Problem (VRP)** — Deciding which vehicle serves which stops in what order to minimize cost under constraints; NP-hard, so solved in practice with heuristics.
segments.tr: - **차량 경로 문제(VRP)** — 제약 조건 아래에서 비용을 최소화하도록 어떤 차량이 어떤 정차지를 어떤 순서로 맡을지 결정하는 문제. NP-난해하므로 실제로는 휴리스틱으로 해결합니다.

segments.src: - **Time window** — A promised delivery interval (e.g., 2–5 p.m.); each one added constrains the route and raises cost.
segments.tr: - **시간창** — 약속된 배송 시간대(예: 오후 2–5시). 하나 추가될 때마다 경로가 제약되고 비용이 올라갑니다.

zh.title: [物流入门 #9] 你的运动鞋跨越大洋只为几个零钱——而最后3英里的成本却更高

segments.src: > Moving freight 8,000 miles is a solved, cheap, standardized problem; moving it the final 3 miles to your porch is the expensive, unsolved one — and the math behind those last 3 miles is genuinely hard.
segments.tr: > 将货物运送8,000英里是一个已解决、低成本且标准化的问题；而把它最后3英里送到你家门廊则是昂贵且尚未解决的问题——这最后3英里背后的数学原理确实很难。

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 今日概念

segments.src: Three ideas do most of the work in modern transportation management.
segments.tr: 三个理念承担了现代运输管理中的大部分工作。

segments.src: Intermodal and multimodal transport.** A shipment rarely uses one mode.
segments.tr: 多式联运（intermodal）与复合运输（multimodal）。** 一批货物很少只使用一种运输方式。

segments.src: It rides a ship, then a truck, then a train, then another truck.
segments.tr: 它先乘船，再乘卡车，接着乘火车，然后再乘一次卡车。

segments.src: The trick that makes this cheap is the **shipping container**: a standardized steel box that gets lifted between modes without anyone touching the goods inside.
segments.tr: 让这一切变得便宜的关键是**集装箱**：一种标准化的钢制箱体，可以在不同运输方式之间吊运，而无需任何人触碰箱内的货物。

segments.src: Load it once in a factory in Vietnam, unload it once at a warehouse in Ohio.
segments.tr: 在越南的工厂装箱一次，在俄亥俄州的仓库卸箱一次。

segments.src: The two words are often used interchangeably, but there's a useful distinction in contracts.
segments.tr: 这两个词常被互换使用，但在合同中有一个有用的区别。

segments.src: *Intermodal* usually describes the physical fact — several modes, one loading unit, often several separate carrier contracts.
segments.tr: *Intermodal* 通常描述的是物理事实——多种运输方式、一个装载单元，通常对应多份独立的承运合同。

segments.src: *Multimodal* usually describes the commercial fact — **one contract, one operator liable for the whole door-to-door journey**, typically under a single through bill of lading.
segments.tr: *Multimodal* 通常描述的是商业事实——**一份合同、一个经营人对门到门的全程负责**，通常在一份全程联运提单下签发。

segments.src: That matters when something goes wrong.
segments.tr: 这在出问题时很重要。

segments.src: Under separate contracts, you have to prove *which* leg damaged the cargo.
segments.tr: 在多份独立合同下，你必须证明*是哪一段*损坏了货物。

segments.src: Under a single multimodal contract, you have one party to call.
segments.tr: 在单一复合运输合同下，你只需找一个责任方。

segments.src: The last mile.** The final leg from a local depot to the customer's door.
segments.tr: 最后一英里。** 从本地配送站到客户门口的最后一段路程。

segments.src: It's the leg where economies of scale collapse.
segments.tr: 这正是规模经济瓦解的一段。

segments.src: A truck leaving the Port of Long Beach carries one container to one place.
segments.tr: 从长滩港驶出的卡车只把一个集装箱运到一个地方。

segments.src: A delivery van carries 120 separate packages to 120 separate addresses, each with its own driveway, elevator, gate code, and dog.
segments.tr: 一辆配送货车要把120个独立包裹送往120个不同地址，每个地址都有各自的车道、电梯、门禁密码和一条狗。

segments.src: Industry studies commonly put last-mile delivery at roughly 40–50% of total parcel logistics cost — the shortest leg, the biggest bill.
segments.tr: 行业研究通常认为，最后一英里配送约占包裹物流总成本的40–50%——路程最短，账单却最大。

segments.src: Two levers dominate last-mile economics:
segments.tr: 两个杠杆主导最后一英里的经济性：

segments.src: - **Stop density** — how many deliveries you make per mile driven. Dense city blocks are cheap per package; rural routes are brutal.
segments.tr: - **停靠密度**——每行驶一英里完成的配送次数。密集的城市街区每件包裹成本低；农村路线则代价高昂。

segments.src: - **First-attempt success rate** — a failed delivery roughly doubles the cost of that package. This is why lockers, pickup points (PUDO), and "leave at door" photos exist. They're not conveniences; they're cost controls.
segments.tr: - **首次投递成功率**——一次投递失败大约会使该包裹的成本翻倍。这就是快递柜、自提点（PUDO）和“放门口”拍照签收存在的原因。它们不是便利设施，而是成本控制手段。

segments.src: The Vehicle Routing Problem (VRP).** Once you have 120 packages and 8 vans, someone has to decide who delivers what, in what order.
segments.tr: 车辆路径问题（VRP）。** 一旦有120个包裹和8辆货车，就必须有人决定谁送什么、以什么顺序送。

segments.src: That's the VRP, formally introduced by Dantzig and Ramser in 1959.
segments.tr: 这就是 VRP，由 Dantzig 和 Ramser 于1959年正式提出。

segments.src: Its simpler cousin is the **Traveling Salesman Problem**: one vehicle, visit every stop once, return home, minimize distance.
segments.tr: 它更简单的近亲是**旅行商问题（TSP）**：一辆车访问每个站点一次，返回出发点，并使总距离最短。

segments.src: TSP is just a VRP with a single uncapacitated vehicle.
segments.tr: TSP 不过是只有一辆、无容量限制车辆的 VRP。

segments.src: Why is this hard?
segments.tr: 为什么这么难？

segments.src: Because the number of possible sequences explodes:
segments.tr: 因为可能的路线顺序会爆炸式增长：

segments.src: 20 stops  ->  20! orderings  ->  about 2,400,000,000,000,000,000 (2.4 quintillion)
segments.tr: 20 stops  ->  20! orderings  ->  about 2,400,000,000,000,000,000 (2.4 quintillion)

segments.src: Checking them all is hopeless, and VRP is **NP-hard** — no known algorithm finds the guaranteed-best answer quickly as the problem grows.
segments.tr: 穷举检验完全不可行，而 VRP 属于 **NP 难问题**——随着问题规模增大，目前没有已知算法能快速找到保证最优的解。

segments.src: Real routing software doesn't look for the perfect route.
segments.tr: 实际的路线规划软件并不寻找完美路线。

segments.src: It uses **heuristics**: rules that find a very good route fast.
segments.tr: 它使用**启发式算法**：即能快速找到非常好路线的规则。

segments.src: The classic is the Clarke–Wright savings algorithm (1964), which asks how much you save by combining two separate out-and-back trips into one:
segments.tr: 经典方法是 Clarke–Wright 节约算法（1964年），它计算的是把两条独立的往返路线合并成一条能节省多少：

segments.src: savings(i, j) = dist(depot, i) + dist(depot, j) - dist(i, j)
segments.tr: savings(i, j) = dist(depot, i) + dist(depot, j) - dist(i, j)

segments.src: Merge the pairs with the biggest savings first, stop when the truck is full.
segments.tr: 优先合并节省量最大的配对，直到货车装满为止。

segments.src: Modern solvers layer on constraints that make it realistic: vehicle capacity, driver hours, and **time windows** — "deliver between 2 and 5 p.m."
segments.tr: 现代求解器还会叠加使其切合实际的约束：车辆容量、司机工时，以及**时间窗**——“下午2点到5点之间送达”。

segments.src: That variant is VRPTW, and every time window you add shrinks the space of legal routes and raises the cost.
segments.tr: 这一变体称为 VRPTW。每增加一个时间窗，合法路线的空间就会缩小，成本随之上升。

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 日常生活中的一例

segments.src: You order a $70 pair of running shoes on a Tuesday night.
segments.tr: 你在一个周二晚上订购了一双70美元的跑鞋。

segments.src: Here's the actual chain:
segments.tr: 以下是实际的链条：

segments.src: The shoes were containerized in Vietnam.
segments.tr: 这双鞋在越南装入了集装箱。

segments.src: A 40-foot container holds several thousand pairs, so at a few thousand dollars for the ocean leg, the trans-Pacific voyage costs well under **$1 per pair** (figures are illustrative and move constantly with market rates).
segments.tr: 一个40英尺集装箱可以装下数千双鞋，因此海运段只需几千美元，跨太平洋航程平摊到每双鞋上远低于**1美元**（数字仅供说明，并随市场运价不断变动）。

segments.src: The box lands at the Port of Los Angeles/Long Beach.
segments.tr: 集装箱抵达洛杉矶/长滩港。

segments.src: A short-haul **drayage** truck hauls it a few miles to a rail ramp — a leg of maybe 20 miles that can cost a few hundred dollars for the container.
segments.tr: 短途的**港区短驳运输（drayage）**卡车把它拖运几英里到铁路货场——这段约20英里的路程，集装箱费用可能只需几百美元。

segments.src: Then a BNSF or Union Pacific intermodal train carries it to the Chicago area, the country's biggest inland rail hub, where a truck takes it to a regional distribution center.
segments.tr: 随后，BNSF 或 Union Pacific 的多式联运列车将其运往芝加哥地区——那是全美最大的内陆铁路枢纽——再由卡车运往区域配送中心。

segments.src: Everything so far was cheap per pair, because everything so far moved *thousands of pairs at once*.
segments.tr: 到目前为止的一切，每双鞋的成本都很低，因为这些环节都是*一次运送数千双鞋*。

segments.src: Then you click "buy."
segments.tr: 然后你点击“购买”。

segments.src: Now one pair, in one box, needs to reach one address.
segments.tr: 现在，一双鞋装在一个箱子里，需要送到一个地址。

segments.src: It gets picked, sorted, trucked to a local delivery station, and loaded onto a van with ~120 other packages.
segments.tr: 它被拣选、分拣，用卡车运到本地配送站，并装上一辆载有约120个其他包裹的货车。

segments.src: That van's driver burns fuel, time, and wages for **your** stop specifically — and the retailer's cost for that final leg is typically several dollars, more than the ocean, rail, and highway legs combined.
segments.tr: 这辆车的司机要为**你的**那一站消耗燃油、时间和工资——而零售商在这最后一段的成本通常是几美元，超过海运、铁路和公路段的总和。

segments.src: This is also why UPS famously routes its drivers to avoid left turns where practical.
segments.tr: 这也是 UPS 著名地在可行时让司机避开左转弯的原因。

segments.src: Waiting to cross oncoming traffic burns fuel and time and raises collision risk.
segments.tr: 等待穿越对向车流既浪费燃油和时间，又会增加碰撞风险。

segments.src: UPS's ORION routing system, rolled out across its U.S.
segments.tr: UPS 的 ORION 路线系统已在其美国

segments.src: network by 2016, applies that logic at scale; the company has said it saves roughly 100 million miles and about 10 million gallons of fuel a year.
segments.tr: 全境网络推广（2016年前完成），把这一逻辑规模化应用；该公司表示，每年可节省约1亿英里里程和约1000万加仑燃油。

segments.src: That's a company figure, not an independent audit — but the direction is real.
segments.tr: 这是公司提供的数字，而非独立审计——但方向是真实的。

segments.src: When you're solving a VRP 55,000 times a day, a small per-stop improvement compounds into a very large number.
segments.tr: 当你每天要求解55,000次 VRP 时，每个停靠点的小幅改进就会累积成非常庞大的数字。

segments.src: ## The 3-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## 三行总结

segments.src: 1. Intermodal/multimodal transport makes long-haul freight absurdly cheap by standardizing the box and never touching the goods — and a single multimodal contract means one party is liable end to end.
segments.tr: 1. 多式联运和复合运输通过标准化集装箱、且从不触碰货物，使长途货运变得极其便宜——而单一复合运输合同意味着由一个责任方对全程负责。

segments.src: 2. The last mile is the shortest and most expensive leg, roughly 40–50% of parcel cost, and it lives or dies on stop density and first-attempt success.
segments.tr: 2. 最后一英里是最短、也最昂贵的一段，约占包裹成本的40–50%，其成败取决于停靠密度和首次投递成功率。

segments.src: 3. Routing that last mile is the Vehicle Routing Problem — NP-hard, so real systems use heuristics for a very good answer rather than searching forever for a perfect one.
segments.tr: 3. 最后一英里的路线规划属于车辆路径问题——它是 NP 难问题，因此实际系统使用启发式算法求得非常好的解，而不是无休止地寻找完美解。

segments.tr: ## ✅ 自测题

segments.tr: 家中，哪一段通常每单位送达成本最*高*？

segments.tr: - (A) 跨太平洋海运航程

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 今日术语

segments.src: - **Intermodal transport** — Moving goods by two or more modes in the same loading unit (usually a container), without handling the goods themselves at transfer points.
segments.tr: - **多式联运（Intermodal transport）** ——在同一装载单元（通常为集装箱）内使用两种或以上运输方式运送货物，且在转运点不直接处理货物本身。

segments.src: - **Multimodal transport** — The commercial version: one contract and one operator responsible for the entire door-to-door journey, typically under a through bill of lading.
segments.tr: - **复合运输（Multimodal transport）** ——其商业形式：由一份合同和一个经营人对门到门的全程运输负责，通常在全程联运提单下签发。

segments.src: - **Drayage** — Short-distance trucking of a container, usually between a port, rail ramp, or nearby warehouse.
segments.tr: - **港区短驳运输（Drayage）** ——集装箱的短途公路运输，通常在港口、铁路货场或附近仓库之间进行。

segments.src: - **Stop density** — Deliveries made per mile driven; the single biggest driver of last-mile cost per package.
segments.tr: - **停靠密度（Stop density）** ——每英里行驶中完成的配送次数；是决定每件包裹最后一英里成本的最大单一因素。

segments.src: - **Vehicle Routing Problem (VRP)** — Deciding which vehicle serves which stops in what order to minimize cost under constraints; NP-hard, so solved in practice with heuristics.
segments.tr: - **车辆路径问题（Vehicle Routing Problem, VRP）** ——在约束条件下决定哪辆车以何种顺序服务哪些站点，以使成本最小；它属于 NP 难问题，因此在实践中用启发式算法求解。

segments.src: - **Time window** — A promised delivery interval (e.g., 2–5 p.m.); each one added constrains the route and raises cost.
segments.tr: - **时间窗（Time window）** ——承诺的送达时段（例如下午2–5点）；每增加一个时间窗都会约束路线并提高成本。

segments.src: *Answers: **Q1 — (C).** The last mile is the shortest leg but carries the least scale, commonly 40–50% of total parcel logistics cost.
segments.tr: *答案：**Q1 — (C)。** 最后一英里是最短的一段，但规模效应最弱，通常占包裹物流总成本的40–50%。

segments.src: **Q2 — O (True).** A VRP with a single vehicle, no capacity limit, and one depot reduces exactly to the TSP.
segments.tr: **Q2 — O（正确）。** 只有一辆车、无容量限制且只有一个配送中心的 VRP 恰好退化为 TSP。

segments.src: **Q3 — (B).** Time windows define the VRPTW variant; capacity limits are already part of the standard capacitated VRP.*
segments.tr: **Q3 — (B)。** 时间窗定义了 VRPTW 这一变体；容量限制本就是标准带容量 VRP 的一部分。*

segments.tr: वह पहले जहाज़ से, फिर ट्रक से, फिर ट्रेन से, और फिर दूसरे ट्रक से चलता है।

segments.src: The trick that makes this cheap is the **shipping container**: a standardized steel box that gets lifted between modes without anyone touching the goods inside.
segments.tr: इसे सस्ता बनाने वाली चाल है **शिपिंग कंटेनर**: एक मानकीकृत स्टील का डिब्बा जिसे बिना सामान को छुए एक माध्यम से दूसरे माध्यम में उठाया जाता है।

segments.src: Load it once in a factory in Vietnam, unload it once at a warehouse in Ohio.
segments.tr: इसे वियतनाम की एक फ़ैक्ट्री में एक बार लोड करें, और ओहायो के एक गोदाम में एक बार उतारें।

segments.src: The two words are often used interchangeably, but there's a useful distinction in contracts.
segments.tr: इन दोनों शब्दों को अक्सर एक-दूसरे की जगह इस्तेमाल किया जाता है, लेकिन अनुबंधों (कॉन्ट्रैक्ट) में इनका एक उपयोगी अंतर है।

segments.src: *Intermodal* usually describes the physical fact — several modes, one loading unit, often several separate carrier contracts.
segments.tr: *इंटरमोडल* आमतौर पर भौतिक तथ्य का वर्णन करता है — कई माध्यम, एक लदान इकाई, और अक्सर कई अलग-अलग कैरियर अनुबंध।

segments.src: *Multimodal* usually describes the commercial fact — **one contract, one operator liable for the whole door-to-door journey**, typically under a single through bill of lading.
segments.tr: *मल्टीमोडल* आमतौर पर व्यावसायिक तथ्य का वर्णन करता है — **एक अनुबंध, एक ऑपरेटर जो पूरी डोर-टू-डोर यात्रा के लिए उत्तरदायी है**, आमतौर पर एक ही थ्रू बिल ऑफ़ लेडिंग के तहत।

segments.src: That matters when something goes wrong.
segments.tr: यह तब मायने रखता है जब कुछ गलत हो जाए।

segments.src: Under separate contracts, you have to prove *which* leg damaged the cargo.
segments.tr: अलग-अलग अनुबंधों के तहत, आपको यह साबित करना होता है कि माल *किस* चरण में क्षतिग्रस्त हुआ।

segments.src: Under a single multimodal contract, you have one party to call.
segments.tr: एक ही मल्टीमोडल अनुबंध के तहत, आपके पास एक ही पक्ष होता है जिससे संपर्क करना है।

segments.src: The last mile.** The final leg from a local depot to the customer's door.
segments.tr: **आख़िरी मील।** स्थानीय डिपो से ग्राहक के दरवाज़े तक का अंतिम चरण।

segments.src: It's the leg where economies of scale collapse.
segments.tr: यही वह चरण है जहाँ पैमाने की बचत (economies of scale) ढह जाती है।

segments.src: A truck leaving the Port of Long Beach carries one container to one place.
segments.tr: लॉन्ग बीच बंदरगाह से निकलने वाला ट्रक एक जगह तक एक ही कंटेनर ले जाता है।

segments.src: A delivery van carries 120 separate packages to 120 separate addresses, each with its own driveway, elevator, gate code, and dog.
segments.tr: एक डिलीवरी वैन 120 अलग-अलग पते पर 120 अलग-अलग पैकेज ले जाती है, और हर पते पर अपना ड्राइववे, लिफ़्ट, गेट कोड और कुत्ता होता है।

segments.src: Industry studies commonly put last-mile delivery at roughly 40–50% of total parcel logistics cost — the shortest leg, the biggest bill.
segments.tr: उद्योग अध्ययन आमतौर पर आख़िरी-मील डिलीवरी को कुल पार्सल लॉजिस्टिक्स लागत का लगभग 40–50% बताते हैं — सबसे छोटा चरण, सबसे बड़ा बिल।

segments.src: Two levers dominate last-mile economics:
segments.tr: आख़िरी-मील की अर्थव्यवस्था पर दो मुख्य लीवर हावी रहते हैं:

segments.src: - **Stop density** — how many deliveries you make per mile driven. Dense city blocks are cheap per package; rural routes are brutal.
segments.tr: - **स्टॉप घनत्व** — चलाए गए हर मील पर आप कितनी डिलीवरी करते हैं। घनी शहरी गलियों में प्रति पैकेज खर्च कम होता है; ग्रामीण मार्ग बहुत महँगे पड़ते हैं।

segments.src: - **First-attempt success rate** — a failed delivery roughly doubles the cost of that package. This is why lockers, pickup points (PUDO), and "leave at door" photos exist. They're not conveniences; they're cost controls.
segments.tr: - **पहली कोशिश में सफलता दर** — असफल डिलीवरी उस पैकेज की लागत लगभग दोगुनी कर देती है। इसीलिए लॉकर, पिकअप पॉइंट (PUDO) और “दरवाज़े पर छोड़ें” वाली फ़ोटो मौजूद हैं। ये सुविधा के लिए नहीं, बल्कि लागत-नियंत्रण के उपाय हैं।

segments.src: The Vehicle Routing Problem (VRP).** Once you have 120 packages and 8 vans, someone has to decide who delivers what, in what order.
segments.tr: **वाहन रूटिंग समस्या (VRP)।** एक बार जब आपके पास 120 पैकेज और 8 वैन हों, तो कोई तय करता है कि कौन क्या डिलीवर करेगा, और किस क्रम में।

segments.src: That's the VRP, formally introduced by Dantzig and Ramser in 1959.
segments.tr: यही VRP है, जिसे औपचारिक रूप से 1959 में Dantzig और Ramser ने प्रस्तुत किया था।

segments.src: Its simpler cousin is the **Traveling Salesman Problem**: one vehicle, visit every stop once, return home, minimize distance.
segments.tr: इसका सरल रूप है **ट्रैवलिंग सेल्समैन समस्या**: एक वाहन, हर स्टॉप पर एक बार जाना, वापस घर लौटना, और दूरी को न्यूनतम करना।

segments.src: TSP is just a VRP with a single uncapacitated vehicle.
segments.tr: TSP बस एक ऐसी VRP है जिसमें एक ही वाहन है और क्षमता की कोई सीमा नहीं।

segments.src: Why is this hard?
segments.tr: यह कठिन क्यों है?

segments.src: Because the number of possible sequences explodes:
segments.tr: क्योंकि संभावित क्रमों की संख्या विस्फोटक रूप से बढ़ जाती है:

segments.src: 20 stops  ->  20! orderings  ->  about 2,400,000,000,000,000,000 (2.4 quintillion)
segments.tr: 20 stops  ->  20! orderings  ->  about 2,400,000,000,000,000,000 (2.4 quintillion)

segments.src: Checking them all is hopeless, and VRP is **NP-hard** — no known algorithm finds the guaranteed-best answer quickly as the problem grows.
segments.tr: उन सभी को जाँचना असंभव है, और VRP **NP-hard** है — कोई ज्ञात एल्गोरिदम नहीं है जो समस्या बढ़ने पर गारंटीशुदा सर्वोत्तम उत्तर जल्दी खोज सके।

segments.src: Real routing software doesn't look for the perfect route.
segments.tr: वास्तविक रूटिंग सॉफ़्टवेयर सही-से-सही रूट नहीं खोजता।

segments.src: It uses **heuristics**: rules that find a very good route fast.
segments.tr: वह **ह्यूरिस्टिक्स** इस्तेमाल करता है: ऐसे नियम जो तेज़ी से बहुत अच्छा रूट ढूँढ लेते हैं।

segments.src: The classic is the Clarke–Wright savings algorithm (1964), which asks how much you save by combining two separate out-and-back trips into one:
segments.tr: इसका क्लासिक उदाहरण है Clarke–Wright बचत एल्गोरिदम (1964), जो पूछता है कि दो अलग-अलग आने-जाने वाली यात्राओं को एक में मिलाने से कितनी बचत होती है:

segments.src: savings(i, j) = dist(depot, i) + dist(depot, j) - dist(i, j)
segments.tr: savings(i, j) = dist(depot, i) + dist(depot, j) - dist(i, j)

segments.src: Merge the pairs with the biggest savings first, stop when the truck is full.
segments.tr: सबसे बड़ी बचत वाली जोड़ियों को पहले मिलाएँ, और ट्रक भर जाने पर रुक जाएँ।

segments.src: Modern solvers layer on constraints that make it realistic: vehicle capacity, driver hours, and **time windows** — "deliver between 2 and 5 p.m."
segments.tr: आधुनिक सॉल्वर इसे व्यावहारिक बनाने के लिए बाधाएँ जोड़ते हैं: वाहन क्षमता, ड्राइवर के घंटे, और **समय-सीमाएँ (time windows)** — “दोपहर 2 से शाम 5 बजे के बीच डिलीवरी करें”।

segments.src: That variant is VRPTW, and every time window you add shrinks the space of legal routes and raises the cost.
segments.tr: इस वेरिएंट को VRPTW कहते हैं, और जोड़ी गई हर समय-सीमा वैध रूटों की जगह को सिकोड़ देती है और लागत बढ़ा देती है।

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## रोज़मर्रा की ज़िंदगी में

segments.src: You order a $70 pair of running shoes on a Tuesday night.
segments.tr: आप मंगलवार रात को $70 के रनिंग शूज़ का ऑर्डर देते हैं।

segments.src: Here's the actual chain:
segments.tr: यह है असली श्रृंखला:

segments.src: The shoes were containerized in Vietnam.
segments.tr: जूतों को वियतनाम में कंटेनराइज़ किया गया।

segments.src: A 40-foot container holds several thousand pairs, so at a few thousand dollars for the ocean leg, the trans-Pacific voyage costs well under **$1 per pair** (figures are illustrative and move constantly with market rates).
segments.tr: एक 40-फ़ुट कंटेनर में कई हज़ार जोड़े आते हैं, इसलिए समुद्री चरण का खर्च कुछ हज़ार डॉलर होने पर, प्रशांत पार की यात्रा का खर्च प्रति जोड़ी **$1 से काफ़ी कम** पड़ता है (आँकड़े उदाहरणात्मक हैं और बाज़ार दरों के साथ लगातार बदलते रहते हैं)।

segments.src: The box lands at the Port of Los Angeles/Long Beach.
segments.tr: डिब्बा लॉस एंजिल्स/लॉन्ग बीच बंदरगाह पर उतरता है।

segments.src: A short-haul **drayage** truck hauls it a few miles to a rail ramp — a leg of maybe 20 miles that can cost a few hundred dollars for the container.
segments.tr: एक छोटी दूरी का **ड्रेएज** ट्रक उसे कुछ मील दूर एक रेल रैंप तक ले जाता है — लगभग 20 मील का यह चरण कंटेनर के लिए कुछ सौ डॉलर पड़ सकता है।

segments.src: Then a BNSF or Union Pacific intermodal train carries it to the Chicago area, the country's biggest inland rail hub, where a truck takes it to a regional distribution center.
segments.tr: फिर एक BNSF या Union Pacific इंटरमोडल ट्रेन उसे शिकागो क्षेत्र तक ले जाती है, जो देश का सबसे बड़ा अंतर्देशीय रेल केंद्र है, और वहाँ से एक ट्रक उसे क्षेत्रीय वितरण केंद्र तक पहुँचाता है।

segments.src: Everything so far was cheap per pair, because everything so far moved *thousands of pairs at once*.
segments.tr: अब तक का हर चरण प्रति जोड़ी सस्ता था, क्योंकि अब तक हर चरण *एक साथ हज़ारों जोड़े* ले जा रहा था।

segments.src: Then you click "buy."
segments.tr: फिर आप “खरीदें” पर क्लिक करते हैं।

segments.src: Now one pair, in one box, needs to reach one address.
segments.tr: अब एक डिब्बे में एक जोड़ी को एक पते तक पहुँचना है।

segments.src: It gets picked, sorted, trucked to a local delivery station, and loaded onto a van with ~120 other packages.
segments.tr: उसे चुना जाता है, छाँटा जाता है, एक स्थानीय डिलीवरी स्टेशन तक ट्रक से ले जाया जाता है, और लगभग 120 अन्य पैकेजों के साथ एक वैन में लोड किया जाता है।

segments.src: That van's driver burns fuel, time, and wages for **your** stop specifically — and the retailer's cost for that final leg is typically several dollars, more than the ocean, rail, and highway legs combined.
segments.tr: उस वैन का ड्राइवर **आपके** स्टॉप के लिए ईंधन, समय और मज़दूरी खर्च करता है — और उस आख़िरी चरण पर खुदरा विक्रेता की लागत आमतौर पर कई डॉलर होती है, जो समुद्री, रेल और हाईवे चरणों की कुल लागत से भी ज़्यादा है।

segments.src: This is also why UPS famously routes its drivers to avoid left turns where practical.
segments.tr: इसीलिए UPS अपने ड्राइवरों को जहाँ संभव हो बाएँ मोड़ से बचने के लिए रूट करने के लिए प्रसिद्ध है।

segments.src: Waiting to cross oncoming traffic burns fuel and time and raises collision risk.
segments.tr: सामने के ट्रैफ़िक को पार करने का इंतज़ार ईंधन और समय खर्च करता है और टक्कर का जोखिम बढ़ाता है।

segments.src: UPS's ORION routing system, rolled out across its U.S.
segments.tr: UPS की ORION रूटिंग प्रणाली, जो 2016 तक अपने पूरे अमेरिकी

segments.src: network by 2016, applies that logic at scale; the company has said it saves roughly 100 million miles and about 10 million gallons of fuel a year.
segments.tr: नेटवर्क में लागू हो गई, इसी तर्क को बड़े पैमाने पर लागू करती है; कंपनी का कहना है कि इससे हर साल लगभग 10 करोड़ मील और लगभग 1 करोड़ गैलन ईंधन बचता है।

segments.src: That's a company figure, not an independent audit — but the direction is real.
segments.tr: यह कंपनी का अपना आँकड़ा है, कोई स्वतंत्र ऑडिट नहीं — लेकिन दिशा सच्ची है।

segments.src: When you're solving a VRP 55,000 times a day, a small per-stop improvement compounds into a very large number.
segments.tr: जब आप दिन में 55,000 बार VRP हल कर रहे हों, तो प्रति स्टॉप छोटा सुधार भी एक बहुत बड़ी संख्या में जुड़ जाता है।

segments.src: ## The 3-Line Recap

1. Intermodal/multimodal transport makes long-haul freight absurdly cheap by standardizing the box and never touching the goods — and a single multimodal contract means one party is liable end to end.
segments.tr: 1. इंटरमोडल/मल्टीमोडल परिवहन मानकीकृत डिब्बे और सामान को कभी न छूने से लंबी दूरी के माल को बेहद सस्ता बनाता है — और एक ही मल्टीमोडल अनुबंध का अर्थ है कि शुरू से अंत तक एक ही पक्ष उत्तरदायी है।

segments.src: 2. The last mile is the shortest and most expensive leg, roughly 40–50% of parcel cost, and it lives or dies on stop density and first-attempt success.
segments.tr: 2. आख़िरी मील सबसे छोटा और सबसे महँगा चरण है, लगभग पार्सल लागत का 40–50%, और यह स्टॉप घनत्व और पहली कोशिश की सफलता पर निर्भर करता है।

segments.src: 3. Routing that last mile is the Vehicle Routing Problem — NP-hard, so real systems use heuristics for a very good answer rather than searching forever for a perfect one.
segments.tr: 3. उस आख़िरी मील की रूटिंग वाहन रूटिंग समस्या है — NP-hard, इसलिए वास्तविक सिस्टम एक पूर्ण उत्तर खोजते रहने के बजाय ह्यूरिस्टिक्स से बहुत अच्छा उत्तर लेते हैं।

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ स्व-प्रश्नोत्तरी

segments.src: **Q1.** For a pair of shoes shipped from Asia to a U.S.
segments.tr: **Q1.** एशिया से अमेरिका के किसी

segments.src: home, which leg typically costs the *most* per unit delivered?
segments.tr: घर तक भेजे गए जूतों की एक जोड़ी के लिए, डिलीवर होने तक प्रति इकाई सबसे *ज़्यादा* खर्च कौन-सा चरण करता है?

segments.src: - (A) The trans-Pacific ocean voyage
segments.tr: - (A) प्रशांत पार समुद्री यात्रा

segments.src: - (B) The intermodal rail move to Chicago
segments.tr: - (B) शिकागो तक इंटरमोडल रेल परिवहन

segments.src: - (C) The final van delivery to your door
segments.tr: - (C) आपके दरवाज़े तक अंतिम वैन डिलीवरी

segments.src: - (D) The drayage move out of the port
segments.tr: - (D) बंदरगाह से ड्रेएज परिवहन

segments.src: **Q2.** O/X: The Traveling Salesman Problem can be described as a special case of the Vehicle Routing Problem.
segments.tr: **Q2.** सही/गलत: ट्रैवलिंग सेल्समैन समस्या को वाहन रूटिंग समस्या की एक विशेष स्थिति के रूप में वर्णित किया जा सकता है।

segments.src: **Q3.** Which change turns a standard VRP into a "VRPTW"?
segments.tr: **Q3.** कौन-सा बदलाव एक मानक VRP को “VRPTW” में बदल देता है?

segments.src: - (A) Adding vehicle capacity limits
segments.tr: - (A) वाहन क्षमता सीमाएँ जोड़ना

segments.src: - (B) Adding customer time windows
segments.tr: - (B) ग्राहक समय-सीमाएँ जोड़ना

segments.src: - (C) Allowing multiple depots

es.title: [Logistics 101 #9] Tus zapatillas cruzaron un océano por unas monedas — Luego, las últimas 3 millas costaron más

segments.src: > Moving freight 8,000 miles is a solved, cheap, standardized problem; moving it the final 3 miles to your porch is the expensive, unsolved one — and the math behind those last 3 miles is genuinely hard.
segments.tr: > Transportar carga 8,000 millas es un problema resuelto, barato y estandarizado; llevarla las últimas 3 millas hasta tu porche es el problema caro y sin resolver, y las matemáticas detrás de esas últimas 3 millas son realmente difíciles.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Concepto de hoy

segments.src: Three ideas do most of the work in modern transportation management.
segments.tr: Tres ideas hacen la mayor parte del trabajo en la gestión moderna del transporte.

segments.src: Intermodal and multimodal transport.** A shipment rarely uses one mode.
segments.tr: Transporte intermodal y multimodal.** Un envío rara vez usa un solo modo.

segments.src: It rides a ship, then a truck, then a train, then another truck.
segments.tr: Viaja en barco, luego en camión, después en tren y finalmente en otro camión.

segments.src: The trick that makes this cheap is the **shipping container**: a standardized steel box that gets lifted between modes without anyone touching the goods inside.
segments.tr: El truco que lo hace barato es el **contenedor de carga**: una caja de acero estandarizada que se levanta entre modos sin que nadie toque las mercancías del interior.

segments.src: Load it once in a factory in Vietnam, unload it once at a warehouse in Ohio.
segments.tr: Se carga una vez en una fábrica en Vietnam y se descarga una vez en un almacén en Ohio.

segments.src: The two words are often used interchangeably, but there's a useful distinction in contracts.
segments.tr: Las dos palabras a menudo se usan indistintamente, pero en los contratos hay una distinción útil.

segments.src: *Intermodal* usually describes the physical fact — several modes, one loading unit, often several separate carrier contracts.
segments.tr: *Intermodal* suele describir el hecho físico: varios modos, una sola unidad de carga, a menudo con varios contratos separados con transportistas.

segments.src: *Multimodal* usually describes the commercial fact — **one contract, one operator liable for the whole door-to-door journey**, typically under a single through bill of lading.
segments.tr: *Multimodal* suele describir el hecho comercial: **un solo contrato, un único operador responsable de todo el trayecto puerta a puerta**, normalmente bajo una única carta de porte directa.

segments.src: That matters when something goes wrong.
segments.tr: Eso importa cuando algo sale mal.

segments.src: Under separate contracts, you have to prove *which* leg damaged the cargo.
segments.tr: Con contratos separados, hay que demostrar *qué* tramo dañó la carga.

segments.src: Under a single multimodal contract, you have one party to call.
segments.tr: Con un único contrato multimodal, hay una sola parte a la que reclamar.

segments.src: The last mile.** The final leg from a local depot to the customer's door.
segments.tr: La última milla.** El tramo final desde un depósito local hasta la puerta del cliente.

segments.src: It's the leg where economies of scale collapse.
segments.tr: Es el tramo en el que las economías de escala se desploman.

segments.src: A truck leaving the Port of Long Beach carries one container to one place.
segments.tr: Un camión que sale del Puerto de Long Beach lleva un contenedor a un solo lugar.

segments.src: A delivery van carries 120 separate packages to 120 separate addresses, each with its own driveway, elevator, gate code, and dog.
segments.tr: Una furgoneta de reparto lleva 120 paquetes separados a 120 direcciones separadas, cada una con su propio acceso, ascensor, código de puerta y perro.

segments.src: Industry studies commonly put last-mile delivery at roughly 40–50% of total parcel logistics cost — the shortest leg, the biggest bill.
segments.tr: Los estudios del sector suelen situar la entrega de última milla en torno al 40–50 % del coste logístico total de los paquetes: el tramo más corto, la factura más grande.

segments.src: Two levers dominate last-mile economics:
segments.tr: Dos palancas dominan la economía de la última milla:

segments.src: - **Stop density** — how many deliveries you make per mile driven. Dense city blocks are cheap per package; rural routes are brutal.
segments.tr: - **Densidad de paradas**: cuántas entregas se realizan por milla recorrida. Las manzanas urbanas densas son baratas por paquete; las rutas rurales son muy costosas.

segments.src: - **First-attempt success rate** — a failed delivery roughly doubles the cost of that package. This is why lockers, pickup points (PUDO), and "leave at door" photos exist. They're not conveniences; they're cost controls.
segments.tr: - **Tasa de éxito en el primer intento**: una entrega fallida casi duplica el coste de ese paquete. Por eso existen las taquillas, los puntos de recogida (PUDO) y las fotos de «dejado en la puerta». No son comodidades; son controles de costes.

segments.src: The Vehicle Routing Problem (VRP).** Once you have 120 packages and 8 vans, someone has to decide who delivers what, in what order.
segments.tr: El problema de enrutamiento de vehículos (VRP).** Una vez que hay 120 paquetes y 8 furgonetas, alguien tiene que decidir quién entrega qué y en qué orden.

segments.src: That's the VRP, formally introduced by Dantzig and Ramser in 1959.
segments.tr: Ese es el VRP, formulado por primera vez por Dantzig y Ramser en 1959.

segments.src: Its simpler cousin is the **Traveling Salesman Problem**: one vehicle, visit every stop once, return home, minimize distance.
segments.tr: Su primo más sencillo es el **problema del viajante de comercio (TSP)**: un vehículo, visitar cada parada una vez, regresar a casa y minimizar la distancia.

segments.src: TSP is just a VRP with a single uncapacitated vehicle.
segments.tr: El TSP es simplemente un VRP con un único vehículo sin límite de capacidad.

segments.src: Why is this hard?
segments.tr: ¿Por qué es difícil?

segments.src: Because the number of possible sequences explodes:
segments.tr: Porque el número de secuencias posibles explota:

segments.src: 20 stops  ->  20! orderings  ->  about 2,400,000,000,000,000,000 (2.4 quintillion)
segments.tr: 20 stops  ->  20! orderings  ->  about 2,400,000,000,000,000,000 (2.4 quintillion)

segments.src: Checking them all is hopeless, and VRP is **NP-hard** — no known algorithm finds the guaranteed-best answer quickly as the problem grows.
segments.tr: Probarlas todas es inviable, y el VRP es **NP-difícil**: ningún algoritmo conocido encuentra la mejor solución garantizada con rapidez a medida que el problema crece.

segments.src: Real routing software doesn't look for the perfect route.
segments.tr: El software de enrutamiento real no busca la ruta perfecta.

segments.src: It uses **heuristics**: rules that find a very good route fast.
segments.tr: Utiliza **heurísticas**: reglas que encuentran una ruta muy buena con rapidez.

segments.src: The classic is the Clarke–Wright savings algorithm (1964), which asks how much you save by combining two separate out-and-back trips into one:
segments.tr: El clásico es el algoritmo de ahorros de Clarke–Wright (1964), que pregunta cuánto se ahorra al combinar dos viajes de ida y vuelta separados en uno:

segments.src: savings(i, j) = dist(depot, i) + dist(depot, j) - dist(i, j)
segments.tr: savings(i, j) = dist(depot, i) + dist(depot, j) - dist(i, j)

segments.src: Merge the pairs with the biggest savings first, stop when the truck is full.
segments.tr: Se fusionan primero los pares con mayores ahorros y se para cuando el camión está lleno.

segments.src: Modern solvers layer on constraints that make it realistic: vehicle capacity, driver hours, and **time windows** — "deliver between 2 and 5 p.m."
segments.tr: Los solucionadores modernos añaden restricciones que lo hacen realista: capacidad del vehículo, horas de conductor y **ventanas horarias**, como «entregar entre las 2 y las 5 p. m.».

segments.src: That variant is VRPTW, and every time window you add shrinks the space of legal routes and raises the cost.
segments.tr: Esa variante es el VRPTW, y cada ventana horaria que se añade reduce el espacio de rutas legales y aumenta el coste.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## En la vida cotidiana

segments.src: You order a $70 pair of running shoes on a Tuesday night.
segments.tr: Un martes por la noche pides un par de zapatillas para correr de 70 $.

segments.src: Here's the actual chain:
segments.tr: Esta es la cadena real:

segments.src: The shoes were containerized in Vietnam.
segments.tr: Las zapatillas se contenerizaron en Vietnam.

segments.src: A 40-foot container holds several thousand pairs, so at a few thousand dollars for the ocean leg, the trans-Pacific voyage costs well under **$1 per pair** (figures are illustrative and move constantly with market rates).
segments.tr: Un contenedor de 40 pies contiene varios miles de pares, así que, con unos pocos miles de dólares por el tramo marítimo, la travesía transpacífica cuesta bastante menos de **1 $ por par** (cifras orientativas que cambian constantemente según las tarifas del mercado).

segments.src: The box lands at the Port of Los Angeles/Long Beach.
segments.tr: La caja llega al Puerto de Los Ángeles/Long Beach.

segments.src: A short-haul **drayage** truck hauls it a few miles to a rail ramp — a leg of maybe 20 miles that can cost a few hundred dollars for the container.
segments.tr: Un camión de **drayage** de corta distancia la transporta unas pocas millas hasta una rampa ferroviaria: un tramo de unas 20 millas que puede costar unos cientos de dólares por contenedor.

segments.src: Then a BNSF or Union Pacific intermodal train carries it to the Chicago area, the country's biggest inland rail hub, where a truck takes it to a regional distribution center.
segments.tr: Después, un tren intermodal de BNSF o Union Pacific la lleva a la zona de Chicago, el mayor centro ferroviario interior del país, donde un camión la traslada a un centro de distribución regional.

segments.src: Everything so far was cheap per pair, because everything so far moved *thousands of pairs at once*.
segments.tr: Todo lo anterior fue barato por par, porque todo lo anterior movió *miles de pares a la vez*.

segments.src: Then you click "buy."
segments.tr: Luego haces clic en «comprar».

segments.src: Now one pair, in one box, needs to reach one address.
segments.tr: Ahora un solo par, en una sola caja, tiene que llegar a una sola dirección.

segments.src: It gets picked, sorted, trucked to a local delivery station, and loaded onto a van with ~120 other packages.
segments.tr: Se recoge, se clasifica, se transporta a una estación de reparto local y se carga en una furgoneta con unos 120 paquetes más.

segments.src: That van's driver burns fuel, time, and wages for **your** stop specifically — and the retailer's cost for that final leg is typically several dollars, more than the ocean, rail, and highway legs combined.
segments.tr: El conductor de esa furgoneta gasta combustible, tiempo y salario para **tu** parada en concreto, y el coste que asume el minorista por ese último tramo suele ser de varios dólares, más que los tramos marítimo, ferroviario y de carretera juntos.

segments.src: This is also why UPS famously routes its drivers to avoid left turns where practical.
segments.tr: Por eso UPS es conocido por diseñar rutas para que sus conductores eviten, cuando es posible, los giros a la izquierda.

segments.src: Waiting to cross oncoming traffic burns fuel and time and raises collision risk.
segments.tr: Esperar para cruzar el tráfico de frente gasta combustible y tiempo, y aumenta el riesgo de colisión.

segments.src: UPS's ORION routing system, rolled out across its U.S.
segments.tr: El sistema de enrutamiento ORION de UPS, desplegado en su red de EE. UU.

segments.src: network by 2016, applies that logic at scale; the company has said it saves roughly 100 million miles and about 10 million gallons of fuel a year.
segments.tr: en 2016, aplica esa lógica a gran escala; la empresa ha afirmado que ahorra unos 100 millones de millas y unos 10 millones de galones de combustible al año.

segments.src: That's a company figure, not an independent audit — but the direction is real.
segments.tr: Es una cifra de la propia empresa, no una auditoría independiente, pero la dirección es real.

segments.src: When you're solving a VRP 55,000 times a day, a small per-stop improvement compounds into a very large number.
segments.tr: Cuando resuelves un VRP 55,000 veces al día, una pequeña mejora por parada se convierte en una cifra enorme.

segments.src: ## The 3-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## El resumen en 3 líneas

segments.src: 1. Intermodal/multimodal transport makes long-haul freight absurdly cheap by standardizing the box and never touching the goods — and a single multimodal contract means one party is liable end to end.
segments.tr: 1. El transporte intermodal/multimodal hace que el flete de larga distancia sea absurdamente barato al estandarizar la caja y no tocar nunca la mercancía; y un único contrato multimodal significa que una sola parte responde de principio a fin.

segments.src: 2. The last mile is the shortest and most expensive leg, roughly 40–50% of parcel cost, and it lives or dies on stop density and first-attempt success.
segments.tr: 2. La última milla es el tramo más corto y más caro, en torno al 40–50 % del coste del paquete, y depende de la densidad de paradas y del éxito en el primer intento.

segments.src: 3. Routing that last mile is the Vehicle Routing Problem — NP-hard, so real systems use heuristics for a very good answer rather than searching forever for a perfect one.
segments.tr: 3. Enrutar esa última milla es el problema de enrutamiento de vehículos: NP-difícil, así que los sistemas reales usan heurísticas para obtener una muy buena solución en lugar de buscar eternamente la perfecta.

segments.src: The trick that makes this cheap is the **shipping container**: a standardized steel box that gets lifted between modes without anyone touching the goods inside.
segments.tr: والحيلة التي تجعل ذلك رخيصًا هي **حاوية الشحن**: صندوق فولاذي موحّد يُرفع بين الوسائط دون أن يلمس أحد البضائع الموجودة داخله.

segments.src: Load it once in a factory in Vietnam, unload it once at a warehouse in Ohio.
segments.tr: تُحمَّل مرة واحدة في مصنع في فيتنام، وتُفرَّغ مرة واحدة في مستودع في أوهايو.

segments.src: The two words are often used interchangeably, but there's a useful distinction in contracts.
segments.tr: غالبًا ما يُستخدم المصطلحان بالتبادل، لكن هناك فرق مفيد في العقود.

segments.src: *Intermodal* usually describes the physical fact — several modes, one loading unit, often several separate carrier contracts.
segments.tr: يصف مصطلح *المتكامل* عادةً الواقع المادي: عدة وسائط ووحدة تحميل واحدة، وغالبًا عدة عقود منفصلة مع ناقلين مختلفين.

segments.src: *Multimodal* usually describes the commercial fact — **one contract, one operator liable for the whole door-to-door journey**, typically under a single through bill of lading.
segments.tr: أما *متعدد الوسائط* فيصف الواقع التجاري عادةً: **عقد واحد ومشغّل واحد مسؤول عن الرحلة كاملة من الباب إلى الباب**، وعادةً بموجب بوليصة شحن واحدة شاملة.

segments.src: That matters when something goes wrong.
segments.tr: وهذا مهم عند حدوث خلل.

segments.src: Under separate contracts, you have to prove *which* leg damaged the cargo.
segments.tr: في ظل عقود منفصلة، يجب أن تُثبت *أي* مرحلة تسببت في تلف البضاعة.

segments.src: Under a single multimodal contract, you have one party to call.
segments.tr: في ظل عقد واحد متعدد الوسائط، يكون لديك طرف واحد تطالبه.

segments.src: The last mile.** The final leg from a local depot to the customer's door.
segments.tr: **الميل الأخير.** المرحلة الأخيرة من المستودع المحلي إلى باب العميل.

segments.src: It's the leg where economies of scale collapse.
segments.tr: وهي المرحلة التي تنهار فيها وفورات الحجم.

segments.src: A truck leaving the Port of Long Beach carries one container to one place.
segments.tr: فالشاحنة التي تغادر ميناء لونغ بيتش تحمل حاوية واحدة إلى مكان واحد.

segments.src: A delivery van carries 120 separate packages to 120 separate addresses, each with its own driveway, elevator, gate code, and dog.
segments.tr: أما شاحنة التوصيل فتحمل 120 طردًا منفصلًا إلى 120 عنوانًا منفصلًا، لكل منها مدخلها الخاص ومصعدها ورمز بوابتها وكلبها.

segments.src: Industry studies commonly put last-mile delivery at roughly 40–50% of total parcel logistics cost — the shortest leg, the biggest bill.
segments.tr: وتُقدّر دراسات الصناعة عادةً أن التوصيل في الميل الأخير يمثل نحو 40–50% من إجمالي تكلفة لوجستيات الطرود: أقصر مرحلة وأكبر فاتورة.

segments.src: Two levers dominate last-mile economics:
segments.tr: هناك عاملان يهيمنان على اقتصاديات الميل الأخير:

segments.src: - **Stop density** — how many deliveries you make per mile driven. Dense city blocks are cheap per package; rural routes are brutal.
segments.tr: - **كثافة التوقفات**: عدد عمليات التسليم لكل ميل تُقطعه. الأحياء المدينية الكثيفة رخيصة لكل طرد، بينما المسارات الريفية مرهقة للغاية.

segments.src: - **First-attempt success rate** — a failed delivery roughly doubles the cost of that package. This is why lockers, pickup points (PUDO), and "leave at door" photos exist. They're not conveniences; they're cost controls.
segments.tr: - **نسبة نجاح المحاولة الأولى**: فشل التسليم يضاعف تقريبًا تكلفة ذلك الطرد. ولهذا توجد الخزائن الذاتية ونقاط الاستلام (PUDO) وصور «الترك عند الباب». فهي ليست وسائل راحة، بل أدوات للتحكم في التكلفة.

segments.src: The Vehicle Routing Problem (VRP).** Once you have 120 packages and 8 vans, someone has to decide who delivers what, in what order.
segments.tr: **مشكلة توجيه المركبات (VRP).** بمجرد أن يكون لديك 120 طردًا و8 شاحنات توصيل، يجب على أحدهم أن يقرر من يوصل ماذا، وبأي ترتيب.

segments.src: That's the VRP, formally introduced by Dantzig and Ramser in 1959.
segments.tr: هذه هي مشكلة VRP، التي قدّمها رياضيًا Dantzig وRamser عام 1959.

segments.src: Its simpler cousin is the **Traveling Salesman Problem**: one vehicle, visit every stop once, return home, minimize distance.
segments.tr: ومشكلتها الأبسط قرينةً هي **مشكلة البائع المتجول**: مركبة واحدة تزور كل توقف مرة واحدة، ثم تعود إلى نقطة الانطلاق، مع تقليل المسافة.

segments.src: TSP is just a VRP with a single uncapacitated vehicle.
segments.tr: ومشكلة البائع المتجول ليست إلا مشكلة VRP بمركبة واحدة غير محدودة السعة.

segments.src: Why is this hard?
segments.tr: لماذا هي صعبة؟

segments.src: Because the number of possible sequences explodes:
segments.tr: لأن عدد التسلسلات الممكنة ينفجر:

segments.src: 20 stops  ->  20! orderings  ->  about 2,400,000,000,000,000,000 (2.4 quintillion)
segments.tr: 20 stops  ->  20! orderings  ->  about 2,400,000,000,000,000,000 (2.4 quintillion)

segments.src: Checking them all is hopeless, and VRP is **NP-hard** — no known algorithm finds the guaranteed-best answer quickly as the problem grows.
segments.tr: ففحصها كلها أمر مستحيل، ومشكلة VRP من فئة **NP-صعبة**، إذ لا توجد خوارزمية معروفة تجد الحل الأفضل المضمون بسرعة مع نمو حجم المشكلة.

segments.src: Real routing software doesn't look for the perfect route.
segments.tr: برمجيات التوجيه الحقيقية لا تبحث عن المسار المثالي.

segments.src: It uses **heuristics**: rules that find a very good route fast.
segments.tr: بل تستخدم **الاستدلالات (heuristics)**: قواعد تجد مسارًا جيدًا جدًا بسرعة.

segments.src: The classic is the Clarke–Wright savings algorithm (1964), which asks how much you save by combining two separate out-and-back trips into one:
segments.tr: والمثال الكلاسيكي هو خوارزمية Clarke–Wright للتوفير (1964)، التي تسأل كم توفر عند دمج رحلتين منفصلتين ذهابًا وإيابًا في رحلة واحدة:

segments.src: savings(i, j) = dist(depot, i) + dist(depot, j) - dist(i, j)
segments.tr: savings(i, j) = dist(depot, i) + dist(depot, j) - dist(i, j)

segments.src: Merge the pairs with the biggest savings first, stop when the truck is full.
segments.tr: ادمج الأزواج ذات أكبر توفير أولًا، وتوقف عندما تمتلئ الشاحنة.

segments.src: Modern solvers layer on constraints that make it realistic: vehicle capacity, driver hours, and **time windows** — "deliver between 2 and 5 p.m."
segments.tr: وتضيف برمجيات الحل الحديثة قيودًا تجعله واقعيًا: سعة المركبة، وساعات عمل السائق، و**النوافذ الزمنية**، مثل «التسليم بين الثانية والخامسة مساءً».

segments.src: That variant is VRPTW, and every time window you add shrinks the space of legal routes and raises the cost.
segments.tr: هذا المتغير يسمى VRPTW، وكل نافذة زمنية تضيفها تُقلّص مجال المسارات المسموحة وترفع التكلفة.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## في الحياة اليومية

segments.src: You order a $70 pair of running shoes on a Tuesday night.
segments.tr: تطلب زوجًا من أحذية الجري بسعر 70 دولارًا ليلة الثلاثاء.

segments.src: Here's the actual chain:
segments.tr: إليك السلسلة الفعلية:

segments.src: The shoes were containerized in Vietnam.
segments.tr: حُمِّلت الأحذية في حاويات في فيتنام.

segments.src: A 40-foot container holds several thousand pairs, so at a few thousand dollars for the ocean leg, the trans-Pacific voyage costs well under **$1 per pair** (figures are illustrative and move constantly with market rates).
segments.tr: الحاوية بطول 40 قدمًا تتسع لعدة آلاف من الأزواج، لذا فعند بضعة آلاف من الدولارات لمرحلة النقل البحري، تكون تكلفة رحلة عبر المحيط الهادئ أقل بكثير من **دولار واحد لكل زوج** (الأرقام توضيحية وتتغير باستمرار مع أسعار السوق).

segments.src: The box lands at the Port of Los Angeles/Long Beach.
segments.tr: تصل الحاوية إلى ميناء لوس أنجلوس/لونغ بيتش.

segments.src: A short-haul **drayage** truck hauls it a few miles to a rail ramp — a leg of maybe 20 miles that can cost a few hundred dollars for the container.
segments.tr: تنقلها شاحنة **Drayage** قصيرة المسافة لبضعة أميال إلى محطة سكك حديد، في مرحلة تبلغ نحو 20 ميلًا وقد تكلّف بضع مئات من الدولارات للحاوية.

segments.src: Then a BNSF or Union Pacific intermodal train carries it to the Chicago area, the country's biggest inland rail hub, where a truck takes it to a regional distribution center.
segments.tr: ثم يحملها قطار متكامل تابع لـ BNSF أو Union Pacific إلى منطقة شيكاغو، أكبر مركز سكك حديد داخلي في البلاد، حيث تنقلها شاحنة إلى مركز توزيع إقليمي.

segments.src: Everything so far was cheap per pair, because everything so far moved *thousands of pairs at once*.
segments.tr: كل ما سبق كان رخيصًا لكل زوج، لأن كل ما سبق نقل *آلاف الأزواج دفعة واحدة*.

segments.src: Then you click "buy."
segments.tr: ثم تنقر على «شراء».

segments.src: Now one pair, in one box, needs to reach one address.
segments.tr: الآن يحتاج زوج واحد، في صندوق واحد، للوصول إلى عنوان واحد.

segments.src: It gets picked, sorted, trucked to a local delivery station, and loaded onto a van with ~120 other packages.
segments.tr: يُلتقط ويُفرز وتنقله شاحنة إلى محطة توصيل محلية، ثم يُحمَّل على شاحنة توصيل مع نحو 120 طردًا آخر.

segments.src: That van's driver burns fuel, time, and wages for **your** stop specifically — and the retailer's cost for that final leg is typically several dollars, more than the ocean, rail, and highway legs combined.
segments.tr: يستهلك سائق تلك الشاحنة الوقود والوقت والأجور من أجل **توقفك** أنت تحديدًا، وتكلفة هذه المرحلة الأخيرة على التاجر عادةً عدة دولارات، أي أكثر من مراحل النقل البحري والسكك الحديدية والطرق السريعة مجتمعة.

segments.src: This is also why UPS famously routes its drivers to avoid left turns where practical.
segments.tr: ولهذا تشتهر UPS بتوجيه سائقيها لتجنب الانعطاف يسارًا حيثما أمكن.

segments.src: Waiting to cross oncoming traffic burns fuel and time and raises collision risk.
segments.tr: فالانتظار لعبور حركة المرور القادمة يستهلك الوقود والوقت ويرفع خطر الحوادث.

segments.src: UPS's ORION routing system, rolled out across its U.S.
segments.tr: يمتد نظام التوجيه ORION التابع لـ UPS، الذي طُرح عبر شبكتها الأمريكية

segments.src: network by 2016, applies that logic at scale; the company has said it saves roughly 100 million miles and about 10 million gallons of fuel a year.
segments.tr: بحلول عام 2016، ويطبّق هذا المنطق على نطاق واسع؛ وتقول الشركة إنه يوفر نحو 100 مليون ميل و10 ملايين غالون من الوقود سنويًا.

segments.src: That's a company figure, not an independent audit — but the direction is real.
segments.tr: وهذا رقم تقدمه الشركة، وليس تدقيقًا مستقلًا، لكن الاتجاه حقيقي.

segments.src: When you're solving a VRP 55,000 times a day, a small per-stop improvement compounds into a very large number.
segments.tr: عندما تحل مشكلة VRP 55,000 مرة يوميًا، يتراكم تحسين صغير في كل توقف ليصبح رقمًا كبيرًا جدًا.

segments.src: ## The 3-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## ملخص في 3 أسطر

segments.src: 1. Intermodal/multimodal transport makes long-haul freight absurdly cheap by standardizing the box and never touching the goods — and a single multimodal contract means one party is liable end to end.
segments.tr: 1. النقل المتكامل ومتعدد الوسائط يجعل الشحن لمسافات طويلة رخيصًا بشكل مدهش عبر توحيد الصندوق وعدم لمس البضاعة أبدًا، وعقد متعدد الوسائط واحد يعني أن طرفًا واحدًا مسؤول من البداية إلى النهاية.

segments.src: 2. The last mile is the shortest and most expensive leg, roughly 40–50% of parcel cost, and it lives or dies on stop density and first-attempt success.
segments.tr: 2. الميل الأخير هو المرحلة الأقصر والأغلى، إذ يمثل نحو 40–50% من تكلفة الطرود، ويعتمد نجاحه على كثافة التوقفات ونجاح المحاولة الأولى.

segments.src: 3. Routing that last mile is the Vehicle Routing Problem — NP-hard, so real systems use heuristics for a very good answer rather than searching forever for a perfect one.
segments.tr: 3. توجيه ذلك الميل الأخير هو مشكلة توجيه المركبات، وهي NP-صعبة، لذا تستخدم الأنظمة العملية استدلالات للوصول إلى حل جيد جدًا بدلًا من البحث إلى الأبد عن الحل المثالي.

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 مصطلحات اليوم

segments.src: - **Intermodal transport** — Moving goods by two or more modes in the same loading unit (usually a container), without handling the goods themselves at transfer points.
segments.tr: - **النقل المتكامل**: نقل البضائع بوسيلتين أو أكثر في وحدة تحميل واحدة (عادةً حاوية)، دون مناولة البضائع نفسها عند نقاط التحويل.

segments.src: - **Multimodal transport** — The commercial version: one contract and one operator responsible for the entire door-to-door journey, typically under a through bill of lading.
segments.tr: - **النقل متعدد الوسائط**: النسخة التجارية، أي عقد واحد ومشغّل واحد مسؤول عن الرحلة كاملة من الباب إلى الباب، وعادةً بموجب بوليصة شحن شاملة.

segments.src: - **Drayage** — Short-distance trucking of a container, usually between a port, rail ramp, or nearby warehouse.
segments.tr: - **Drayage**: نقل الحاويات بالشاحنات لمسافات قصيرة، عادةً بين ميناء أو محطة سكك حديد أو مستودع قريب.

segments.src: - **Stop density** — Deliveries made per mile driven; the single biggest driver of last-mile cost per package.
segments.tr: - **كثافة التوقفات**: عدد عمليات التسليم لكل ميل مقطوع، وهي أكبر عامل منفرد يحدد تكلفة الميل الأخير لكل طرد.

segments.src: - **Vehicle Routing Problem (VRP)** — Deciding which vehicle serves which stops in what order to minimize cost under constraints; NP-hard, so solved in practice with heuristics.
segments.tr: - **مشكلة توجيه المركبات (VRP)**: تحديد المركبة التي تخدم كل توقف، وبأي ترتيب، لتقليل التكلفة ضمن القيود. وهي NP-صعبة، لذا تُحل عمليًا بالاستدلالات.

segments.src: - **Time window** — A promised delivery interval (e.g., 2–5 p.m.); each one added constrains the route and raises cost.
segments.tr: - **النافذة الزمنية**: فترة تسليم موعودة (مثل 2–5 مساءً)، وكل نافذة تُضاف تقيّد المسار وترفع التكلفة.

segments.src: *Answers: **Q1 — (C).** The last mile is the shortest leg but carries the least scale, commonly 40–50% of total parcel logistics cost.
segments.tr: *الإجابات: **س1 — (ج).** الميل الأخير هو الأقصر لكن يحمل أقل قدر من الحجم، ويمثل عادةً 40–50% من إجمالي تكلفة لوجستيات الطرود.

segments.src: **Q2 — O (True).** A VRP with a single vehicle, no capacity limit, and one depot reduces exactly to the TSP.
segments.tr: **س2 — O (صح).** مشكلة VRP بمركبة واحدة وبلا حد للسعة ومستودع واحد تختزل تمامًا إلى مشكلة البائع المتجول.

segments.src: **Q3 — (B).** Time windows define the VRPTW variant; capacity limits are already part of the standard capacitated VRP.*
segments.tr: **س3 — (ب).** النوافذ الزمنية تحدد متغير VRPTW، أما حدود السعة فهي موجودة بالفعل ضمن مشكلة VRP ذات السعة القياسية.*

segments.src: > Moving freight 8,000 miles is a solved, cheap, standardized problem; moving it the final 3 miles to your porch is the expensive, unsolved one — and the math behind those last 3 miles is genuinely hard.
segments.tr: > Transporter du fret sur 8 000 miles est un problème résolu, bon marché et standardisé ; le transporter sur les 3 derniers miles jusqu'à votre perron est le problème coûteux, non résolu — et les calculs derrière ces 3 derniers miles sont réellement difficiles.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Concept du jour

segments.src: Three ideas do most of the work in modern transportation management.
segments.tr: Trois idées portent l'essentiel du travail dans la gestion moderne des transports.

segments.src: Intermodal and multimodal transport.** A shipment rarely uses one mode.
segments.tr: Transport intermodal et multimodal.** Une expédition n'emprunte que rarement un seul mode.

segments.src: It rides a ship, then a truck, then a train, then another truck.
segments.tr: Elle voyage sur un navire, puis un camion, puis un train, puis encore un camion.

segments.src: The trick that makes this cheap is the **shipping container**: a standardized steel box that gets lifted between modes without anyone touching the goods inside.
segments.tr: Ce qui rend le procédé bon marché, c'est le **conteneur maritime** : une caisse en acier standardisée, soulevée d'un mode à l'autre sans que personne ne touche aux marchandises qu'elle contient.

segments.src: Load it once in a factory in Vietnam, unload it once at a warehouse in Ohio.
segments.tr: On le charge une seule fois dans une usine au Vietnam, et on le décharge une seule fois dans un entrepôt de l'Ohio.

segments.src: The two words are often used interchangeably, but there's a useful distinction in contracts.
segments.tr: Ces deux termes sont souvent employés comme synonymes, mais les contrats font une distinction utile.

segments.src: *Intermodal* usually describes the physical fact — several modes, one loading unit, often several separate carrier contracts.
segments.tr: *Intermodal* désigne en général le fait physique : plusieurs modes, une seule unité de chargement, souvent plusieurs contrats de transporteurs distincts.

segments.src: *Multimodal* usually describes the commercial fact — **one contract, one operator liable for the whole door-to-door journey**, typically under a single through bill of lading.
segments.tr: *Multimodal* désigne en général le fait commercial : **un seul contrat, un seul opérateur responsable de tout le trajet de porte à porte**, généralement sous un connaissement direct unique.

segments.src: That matters when something goes wrong.
segments.tr: Cela compte lorsque quelque chose tourne mal.

segments.src: Under separate contracts, you have to prove *which* leg damaged the cargo.
segments.tr: Avec des contrats séparés, il faut prouver *quel* tronçon a endommagé la marchandise.

segments.src: Under a single multimodal contract, you have one party to call.
segments.tr: Avec un contrat multimodal unique, il n'y a qu'un seul interlocuteur à appeler.

segments.src: The last mile.** The final leg from a local depot to the customer's door.
segments.tr: Le dernier kilomètre.** Le tronçon final, du dépôt local jusqu'à la porte du client.

segments.src: It's the leg where economies of scale collapse.
segments.tr: C'est le tronçon où les économies d'échelle s'effondrent.

segments.src: A truck leaving the Port of Long Beach carries one container to one place.
segments.tr: Un camion quittant le port de Long Beach transporte un conteneur vers un seul lieu.

segments.src: A delivery van carries 120 separate packages to 120 separate addresses, each with its own driveway, elevator, gate code, and dog.
segments.tr: Une camionnette de livraison transporte 120 colis distincts vers 120 adresses distinctes, chacune avec son allée, son ascenseur, son code de portail et son chien.

segments.src: Industry studies commonly put last-mile delivery at roughly 40–50% of total parcel logistics cost — the shortest leg, the biggest bill.
segments.tr: Les études du secteur évaluent couramment la livraison du dernier kilomètre à environ 40 à 50 % du coût logistique total des colis : le tronçon le plus court, la facture la plus lourde.

segments.src: Two levers dominate last-mile economics:
segments.tr: Deux leviers dominent l'économie du dernier kilomètre :

segments.src: - **Stop density** — how many deliveries you make per mile driven. Dense city blocks are cheap per package; rural routes are brutal.
segments.tr: - **Densité d'arrêts** — le nombre de livraisons effectuées par mile parcouru. Les quartiers urbains denses sont peu coûteux par colis ; les tournées rurales sont brutales.

segments.src: - **First-attempt success rate** — a failed delivery roughly doubles the cost of that package. This is why lockers, pickup points (PUDO), and "leave at door" photos exist. They're not conveniences; they're cost controls.
segments.tr: - **Taux de réussite dès la première tentative** — une livraison échouée double à peu près le coût du colis concerné. C'est pour cela qu'existent les consignes automatiques, les points de retrait (PUDO) et les photos « déposé devant la porte ». Ce ne sont pas des commodités : ce sont des outils de maîtrise des coûts.

segments.src: The Vehicle Routing Problem (VRP).** Once you have 120 packages and 8 vans, someone has to decide who delivers what, in what order.
segments.tr: Le problème de tournée de véhicules (VRP).** Une fois qu'on dispose de 120 colis et de 8 camionnettes, quelqu'un doit décider qui livre quoi, et dans quel ordre.

segments.src: That's the VRP, formally introduced by Dantzig and Ramser in 1959.
segments.tr: C'est le VRP, formellement introduit par Dantzig et Ramser en 1959.

segments.src: Its simpler cousin is the **Traveling Salesman Problem**: one vehicle, visit every stop once, return home, minimize distance.
segments.tr: Son cousin plus simple est le **problème du voyageur de commerce** : un seul véhicule, visiter chaque arrêt une fois, revenir au point de départ, minimiser la distance.

segments.src: TSP is just a VRP with a single uncapacitated vehicle.
segments.tr: Le TSP n'est qu'un VRP avec un seul véhicule sans limite de capacité.

segments.src: Why is this hard?
segments.tr: Pourquoi est-ce difficile ?

segments.src: Because the number of possible sequences explodes:
segments.tr: Parce que le nombre de séquences possibles explose :

segments.src: 20 stops  ->  20! orderings  ->  about 2,400,000,000,000,000,000 (2.4 quintillion)
segments.tr: 20 stops  ->  20! orderings  ->  about 2,400,000,000,000,000,000 (2.4 quintillion)

segments.src: Checking them all is hopeless, and VRP is **NP-hard** — no known algorithm finds the guaranteed-best answer quickly as the problem grows.
segments.tr: Les vérifier toutes est hors de portée, et le VRP est **NP-difficile** : aucun algorithme connu ne trouve rapidement la solution optimale garantie lorsque le problème grandit.

segments.src: Real routing software doesn't look for the perfect route.
segments.tr: Les logiciels de routage réels ne cherchent pas la tournée parfaite.

segments.src: It uses **heuristics**: rules that find a very good route fast.
segments.tr: Ils utilisent des **heuristiques** : des règles qui trouvent très vite une très bonne tournée.

segments.src: The classic is the Clarke–Wright savings algorithm (1964), which asks how much you save by combining two separate out-and-back trips into one:
segments.tr: L'exemple classique est l'algorithme des économies de Clarke et Wright (1964), qui calcule ce que l'on gagne en combinant deux trajets aller-retour séparés en un seul :

segments.src: savings(i, j) = dist(depot, i) + dist(depot, j) - dist(i, j)
segments.tr: savings(i, j) = dist(depot, i) + dist(depot, j) - dist(i, j)

segments.src: Merge the pairs with the biggest savings first, stop when the truck is full.
segments.tr: On fusionne d'abord les couples offrant les plus grandes économies, et on s'arrête lorsque le camion est plein.

segments.src: Modern solvers layer on constraints that make it realistic: vehicle capacity, driver hours, and **time windows** — "deliver between 2 and 5 p.m."
segments.tr: Les solveurs modernes ajoutent des contraintes qui rendent le problème réaliste : capacité des véhicules, temps de conduite des chauffeurs et **fenêtres horaires** — « livrer entre 14 h et 17 h ».

segments.src: That variant is VRPTW, and every time window you add shrinks the space of legal routes and raises the cost.
segments.tr: Cette variante est le VRPTW, et chaque fenêtre horaire ajoutée réduit l'ensemble des tournées admissibles et fait monter le coût.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Dans la vie de tous les jours

segments.src: Then a BNSF or Union Pacific intermodal train carries it to the Chicago area, the country's biggest inland rail hub, where a truck takes it to a regional distribution center.
segments.tr: Puis un train intermodal de BNSF ou d'Union Pacific l'achemine vers la région de Chicago, le plus grand nœud ferroviaire intérieur du pays, où un camion le conduit jusqu'à un centre de distribution régional.

segments.src: Everything so far was cheap per pair, because everything so far moved *thousands of pairs at once*.
segments.tr: Tout ce qui précède était bon marché par paire, parce que tout ce qui précède déplaçait *des milliers de paires à la fois*.

segments.src: Then you click "buy."
segments.tr: Puis vous cliquez sur « acheter ».

segments.src: That van's driver burns fuel, time, and wages for **your** stop specifically — and the retailer's cost for that final leg is typically several dollars, more than the ocean, rail, and highway legs combined.

segments.tr: Attendre pour traverser la circulation venant en face consomme du carburant et du temps, et augmente le risque de collision.

segments.src: ## The 3-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## Récapitulatif en 3 lignes

segments.src: 1. Intermodal/multimodal transport makes long-haul freight absurdly cheap by standardizing the box and never touching the goods — and a single multimodal contract means one party is liable end to end.
segments.tr: 1. Le transport intermodal/multimodal rend le fret longue distance incroyablement bon marché en standardisant la caisse et en ne touchant jamais aux marchandises — et un contrat multimodal unique signifie qu'une seule partie est responsable de bout en bout.

segments.src: 2. The last mile is the shortest and most expensive leg, roughly 40–50% of parcel cost, and it lives or dies on stop density and first-attempt success.
segments.tr: 2. Le dernier kilomètre est le tronçon le plus court et le plus coûteux, environ 40 à 50 % du coût d'un colis, et son sort dépend de la densité d'arrêts et du taux de réussite dès la première tentative.

segments.src: 3. Routing that last mile is the Vehicle Routing Problem — NP-hard, so real systems use heuristics for a very good answer rather than searching forever for a perfect one.
segments.tr: 3. Le routage de ce dernier kilomètre relève du problème de tournée de véhicules — NP-difficile, donc les systèmes réels utilisent des heuristiques pour obtenir une très bonne réponse plutôt que de chercher indéfiniment la solution parfaite.
