segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Termes du jour

segments.src: - **Intermodal transport** — Moving goods by two or more modes in the same loading unit (usually a container), without handling the goods themselves at transfer points.
segments.tr: - **Transport intermodal** — Déplacement de marchandises par deux modes de transport ou plus dans la même unité de chargement (généralement un conteneur), sans manipulation des marchandises elles-mêmes aux points de transfert.

segments.src: - **Multimodal transport** — The commercial version: one contract and one operator responsible for the entire door-to-door journey, typically under a through bill of lading.
segments.tr: - **Transport multimodal** — La version commerciale : un seul contrat et un seul opérateur responsable de tout le trajet de porte à porte, généralement sous un connaissement direct.

segments.src: - **Drayage** — Short-distance trucking of a container, usually between a port, rail ramp, or nearby warehouse.
segments.tr: - **Drayage** — Transport routier sur courte distance d'un conteneur, généralement entre un port, un terminal ferroviaire ou un entrepôt voisin.

segments.src: - **Stop density** — Deliveries made per mile driven; the single biggest driver of last-mile cost per package.
segments.tr: - **Densité d'arrêts** — Livraisons effectuées par mile parcouru ; le facteur le plus déterminant du coût du dernier kilomètre par colis.

segments.src: - **Vehicle Routing Problem (VRP)** — Deciding which vehicle serves which stops in what order to minimize cost under constraints; NP-hard, so solved in practice with heuristics.
segments.tr: - **Problème de tournée de véhicules (VRP)** — Décider quel véhicule dessert quels arrêts et dans quel ordre pour minimiser le coût sous contraintes ; NP-difficile, donc résolu en pratique avec des heuristiques.

segments.src: - **Time window** — A promised delivery interval (e.g., 2–5 p.m.); each one added constrains the route and raises cost.
segments.tr: - **Fenêtre horaire** — Plage horaire de livraison promise (par ex. 14 h–17 h) ; chaque fenêtre ajoutée contraint la tournée et fait monter le coût.

segments.src: 1. Intermodal/multimodal transport makes long-haul freight absurdly cheap by standardizing the box and never touching the goods — and a single multimodal contract means one party is liable end to end.

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Termos de Hoje

segments.src: - **Intermodal transport** — Moving goods by two or more modes in the same loading unit (usually a container), without handling the goods themselves at transfer points.
segments.tr: - **Transporte intermodal** — Movimentação de mercadorias por dois ou mais modais na mesma unidade de carga (geralmente um contêiner), sem manusear as mercadorias em si nos pontos de transferência.

segments.src: - **Multimodal transport** — The commercial version: one contract and one operator responsible for the entire door-to-door journey, typically under a through bill of lading.
segments.tr: - **Transporte multimodal** — A versão comercial: um contrato e um operador responsável por toda a viagem porta a porta, normalmente sob um conhecimento de embarque direto (through bill of lading).

segments.src: - **Drayage** — Short-distance trucking of a container, usually between a port, rail ramp, or nearby warehouse.
segments.tr: - **Drayage** — Transporte rodoviário de curta distância de um contêiner, geralmente entre um porto, um pátio ferroviário ou um armazém próximo.

segments.src: - **Stop density** — Deliveries made per mile driven; the single biggest driver of last-mile cost per package.
segments.tr: - **Densidade de paradas** — Entregas realizadas por milha rodada; o fator isolado mais importante do custo por pacote na última milha.

segments.src: - **Vehicle Routing Problem (VRP)** — Deciding which vehicle serves which stops in what order to minimize cost under constraints; NP-hard, so solved in practice with heuristics.
segments.tr: - **Problema de Roteirização de Veículos (VRP)** — Decidir qual veículo atende quais paradas, e em que ordem, para minimizar o custo sob restrições; NP-difícil, por isso é resolvido na prática com heurísticas.

segments.src: - **Time window** — A promised delivery interval (e.g., 2–5 p.m.); each one added constrains the route and raises cost.
segments.tr: - **Janela de tempo** — Um intervalo de entrega prometido (ex.: 14h–17h); cada janela adicionada restringe a rota e aumenta o custo.

in.title: [Logistik 101 #9] Sepatu Anda Menyeberangi Samudra demi Uang Recehan — Lalu 3 Mil Terakhir Justru Lebih Mahal

segments.src: > Moving freight 8,000 miles is a solved, cheap, standardized problem; moving it the final 3 miles to your porch is the expensive, unsolved one — and the math behind those last 3 miles is genuinely hard.
segments.tr: > Memindahkan kargo sejauh 8.000 mil adalah masalah yang sudah terpecahkan, murah, dan terstandarisasi; memindahkannya 3 mil terakhir sampai ke teras rumah Anda adalah bagian yang mahal dan belum terpecahkan — dan perhitungan di balik 3 mil terakhir itu benar-benar sulit.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Konsep Hari Ini

segments.src: Three ideas do most of the work in modern transportation management.
segments.tr: Tiga gagasan melakukan sebagian besar pekerjaan dalam manajemen transportasi modern.

segments.src: Intermodal and multimodal transport.** A shipment rarely uses one mode.
segments.tr: Transportasi intermoda dan multimoda.** Sebuah pengiriman jarang menggunakan satu moda saja.

segments.src: It rides a ship, then a truck, then a train, then another truck.
segments.tr: Barang itu naik kapal, lalu truk, lalu kereta, lalu truk lagi.

segments.src: The trick that makes this cheap is the **shipping container**: a standardized steel box that gets lifted between modes without anyone touching the goods inside.
segments.tr: Trik yang membuatnya murah adalah **kontainer pengiriman**: kotak baja terstandar yang diangkat antarmoda tanpa seorang pun menyentuh barang di dalamnya.

segments.src: Load it once in a factory in Vietnam, unload it once at a warehouse in Ohio.
segments.tr: Muat sekali di pabrik di Vietnam, bongkar sekali di gudang di Ohio.

segments.src: The two words are often used interchangeably, but there's a useful distinction in contracts.
segments.tr: Kedua istilah ini sering dipakai secara bergantian, tetapi ada perbedaan yang berguna dalam kontrak.

segments.src: *Intermodal* usually describes the physical fact — several modes, one loading unit, often several separate carrier contracts.
segments.tr: *Intermoda* biasanya menggambarkan fakta fisik — beberapa moda, satu unit pemuatan, sering kali dengan beberapa kontrak pengangkut yang terpisah.

segments.src: *Multimodal* usually describes the commercial fact — **one contract, one operator liable for the whole door-to-door journey**, typically under a single through bill of lading.
segments.tr: *Multimoda* biasanya menggambarkan fakta komersial — **satu kontrak, satu operator bertanggung jawab atas seluruh perjalanan dari pintu ke pintu**, umumnya di bawah satu surat muatan (bill of lading) menyeluruh.

segments.src: That matters when something goes wrong.
segments.tr: Itu penting ketika terjadi masalah.

segments.src: Under separate contracts, you have to prove *which* leg damaged the cargo.
segments.tr: Dengan kontrak terpisah, Anda harus membuktikan *bagian mana* yang merusak kargo.

segments.src: Under a single multimodal contract, you have one party to call.
segments.tr: Dengan satu kontrak multimoda, Anda hanya perlu menghubungi satu pihak.

segments.src: The last mile.** The final leg from a local depot to the customer's door.
segments.tr: **Mil terakhir.** Tahap final dari depo lokal ke pintu pelanggan.

segments.src: It's the leg where economies of scale collapse.
segments.tr: Ini adalah tahap di mana skala ekonomi runtuh.

segments.src: A truck leaving the Port of Long Beach carries one container to one place.
segments.tr: Truk yang meninggalkan Pelabuhan Long Beach membawa satu kontainer ke satu tempat.

segments.src: A delivery van carries 120 separate packages to 120 separate addresses, each with its own driveway, elevator, gate code, and dog.
segments.tr: Van pengantar membawa 120 paket terpisah ke 120 alamat terpisah, masing-masing dengan jalan masuk, lift, kode gerbang, dan anjingnya sendiri.

segments.src: Industry studies commonly put last-mile delivery at roughly 40–50% of total parcel logistics cost — the shortest leg, the biggest bill.
segments.tr: Studi industri umumnya memperkirakan pengiriman mil terakhir sekitar 40–50% dari total biaya logistik parsel — tahap terpendek, tagihan terbesar.

segments.src: Two levers dominate last-mile economics:
segments.tr: Dua faktor utama menentukan ekonomi mil terakhir:

segments.src: - **Stop density** — how many deliveries you make per mile driven. Dense city blocks are cheap per package; rural routes are brutal.
segments.tr: - **Kepadatan pemberhentian** — berapa banyak pengiriman yang Anda lakukan per mil yang ditempuh. Blok kota yang padat murah per paket; rute pedesaan sangat berat.

segments.src: - **First-attempt success rate** — a failed delivery roughly doubles the cost of that package. This is why lockers, pickup points (PUDO), and "leave at door" photos exist. They're not conveniences; they're cost controls.
segments.tr: - **Tingkat keberhasilan percobaan pertama** — pengiriman yang gagal kira-kira menggandakan biaya paket tersebut. Inilah alasan loker, titik pengambilan (PUDO), dan foto "tinggalkan di depan pintu" ada. Itu bukan kemudahan; itu pengendali biaya.

segments.src: The Vehicle Routing Problem (VRP).** Once you have 120 packages and 8 vans, someone has to decide who delivers what, in what order.
segments.tr: **Vehicle Routing Problem (VRP).** Begitu Anda punya 120 paket dan 8 van, seseorang harus memutuskan siapa mengantar apa, dan dalam urutan apa.

segments.src: That's the VRP, formally introduced by Dantzig and Ramser in 1959.
segments.tr: Itulah VRP, yang secara formal diperkenalkan oleh Dantzig dan Ramser pada 1959.

segments.src: Its simpler cousin is the **Traveling Salesman Problem**: one vehicle, visit every stop once, return home, minimize distance.
segments.tr: Sepupunya yang lebih sederhana adalah **Traveling Salesman Problem**: satu kendaraan, kunjungi setiap pemberhentian sekali, kembali ke rumah, minimalkan jarak.

segments.src: TSP is just a VRP with a single uncapacitated vehicle.
segments.tr: TSP hanyalah VRP dengan satu kendaraan tanpa batas kapasitas.

segments.src: Why is this hard?
segments.tr: Mengapa ini sulit?

segments.src: Because the number of possible sequences explodes:
segments.tr: Karena jumlah kemungkinan urutan meledak:

segments.src: 20 stops  ->  20! orderings  ->  about 2,400,000,000,000,000,000 (2.4 quintillion)
segments.tr: 20 stops  ->  20! orderings  ->  about 2,400,000,000,000,000,000 (2.4 quintillion)

segments.src: Checking them all is hopeless, and VRP is **NP-hard** — no known algorithm finds the guaranteed-best answer quickly as the problem grows.
segments.tr: Memeriksa semuanya itu sia-sia, dan VRP adalah **NP-hard** — tidak ada algoritma yang diketahui yang dapat menemukan jawaban terbaik yang dijamin dengan cepat seiring bertambahnya masalah.

segments.src: Real routing software doesn't look for the perfect route.
segments.tr: Perangkat lunak routing sungguhan tidak mencari rute yang sempurna.

segments.src: It uses **heuristics**: rules that find a very good route fast.
segments.tr: Ia menggunakan **heuristik**: aturan yang menemukan rute yang sangat baik dengan cepat.

segments.src: The classic is the Clarke–Wright savings algorithm (1964), which asks how much you save by combining two separate out-and-back trips into one:
segments.tr: Yang klasik adalah algoritma penghematan Clarke–Wright (1964), yang menanyakan seberapa banyak Anda menghemat dengan menggabungkan dua perjalanan pulang-pergi yang terpisah menjadi satu:

segments.src: savings(i, j) = dist(depot, i) + dist(depot, j) - dist(i, j)
segments.tr: savings(i, j) = dist(depot, i) + dist(depot, j) - dist(i, j)

segments.src: Merge the pairs with the biggest savings first, stop when the truck is full.
segments.tr: Gabungkan pasangan dengan penghematan terbesar terlebih dahulu, berhenti saat truk penuh.

segments.src: Modern solvers layer on constraints that make it realistic: vehicle capacity, driver hours, and **time windows** — "deliver between 2 and 5 p.m."
segments.tr: Solver modern menambahkan batasan yang membuatnya realistis: kapasitas kendaraan, jam kerja pengemudi, dan **jendela waktu** — "antar antara pukul 2 dan 5 sore".

segments.src: That variant is VRPTW, and every time window you add shrinks the space of legal routes and raises the cost.
segments.tr: Varian itu disebut VRPTW, dan setiap jendela waktu yang Anda tambahkan mempersempit ruang rute yang sah dan menaikkan biaya.

segments.src: - **Intermodal transport** — Moving goods by two or more modes in the same loading unit (usually a container), without handling the goods themselves at transfer points.
segments.tr: - **Transportasi intermoda** — Memindahkan barang dengan dua moda atau lebih dalam unit pemuatan yang sama (biasanya kontainer), tanpa menangani barang itu sendiri di titik transfer.

segments.src: - **Multimodal transport** — The commercial version: one contract and one operator responsible for the entire door-to-door journey, typically under a through bill of lading.
segments.tr: - **Transportasi multimoda** — Versi komersialnya: satu kontrak dan satu operator bertanggung jawab atas seluruh perjalanan dari pintu ke pintu, umumnya di bawah surat muatan menyeluruh.

segments.src: - **Drayage** — Short-distance trucking of a container, usually between a port, rail ramp, or nearby warehouse.
segments.tr: - **Drayage** — Pengangkutan truk jarak pendek untuk kontainer, biasanya antara pelabuhan, jalur rel, atau gudang terdekat.

segments.src: - **Stop density** — Deliveries made per mile driven; the single biggest driver of last-mile cost per package.
segments.tr: - **Kepadatan pemberhentian** — Pengiriman yang dilakukan per mil yang ditempuh; faktor tunggal terbesar yang menentukan biaya mil terakhir per paket.

segments.src: - **Vehicle Routing Problem (VRP)** — Deciding which vehicle serves which stops in what order to minimize cost under constraints; NP-hard, so solved in practice with heuristics.
segments.tr: - **Vehicle Routing Problem (VRP)** — Menentukan kendaraan mana melayani pemberhentian mana dan dalam urutan apa untuk meminimalkan biaya di bawah batasan; NP-hard, sehingga dipecahkan dalam praktik dengan heuristik.

segments.src: - **Time window** — A promised delivery interval (e.g., 2–5 p.m.); each one added constrains the route and raises cost.
segments.tr: - **Jendela waktu** — Interval pengiriman yang dijanjikan (mis., pukul 2–5 sore); setiap jendela yang ditambahkan membatasi rute dan menaikkan biaya.

segments.src: *Answers: **Q1 — (C).** The last mile is the shortest leg but carries the least scale, commonly 40–50% of total parcel logistics cost.
segments.tr: *Jawaban: **Q1 — (C).** Mil terakhir adalah tahap terpendek tetapi memiliki skala paling kecil, umumnya 40–50% dari total biaya logistik parsel.

segments.src: **Q2 — O (True).** A VRP with a single vehicle, no capacity limit, and one depot reduces exactly to the TSP.
segments.tr: **Q2 — B (Benar).** VRP dengan satu kendaraan, tanpa batas kapasitas, dan satu depo tereduksi persis menjadi TSP.

segments.src: **Q3 — (B).** Time windows define the VRPTW variant; capacity limits are already part of the standard capacitated VRP.*
segments.tr: **Q3 — (B).** Jendela waktu mendefinisikan varian VRPTW; batas kapasitas sudah menjadi bagian dari VRP berkapasitas standar.*

ja.title: [物流101 #9] スニーカーは小銭で海を越えた——ところがラストマイルの3マイルのほうが高くつく

segments.src: > Moving freight 8,000 miles is a solved, cheap, standardized problem; moving it the final 3 miles to your porch is the expensive, unsolved one — and the math behind those last 3 miles is genuinely hard.
segments.tr: > 8,000マイルの貨物輸送は、解決済みで安価かつ標準化された問題です。一方、最後の3マイル、つまり玄関先までの輸送は、高価で未解決の問題です。そして、その最後の3マイルの計算は本当に難しいのです。

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 今日のコンセプト

segments.src: Three ideas do most of the work in modern transportation management.
segments.tr: 現代の輸送管理の大部分は、3つの考え方によって成り立っています。

segments.src: Intermodal and multimodal transport.** A shipment rarely uses one mode.
segments.tr: 複合一貫輸送とマルチモーダル輸送。** 貨物が1つの輸送モードだけを使うことはほとんどありません。

segments.src: It rides a ship, then a truck, then a train, then another truck.
segments.tr: 船に乗り、次にトラック、次に列車、さらにもう一台のトラックへと移ります。

segments.src: The trick that makes this cheap is the **shipping container**: a standardized steel box that gets lifted between modes without anyone touching the goods inside.
segments.tr: これを安価にする仕組みが**海上コンテナ**です。標準化された鋼鉄製の箱で、中の貨物に誰も触れることなく、輸送モード間で持ち上げて移し替えられます。

segments.src: Load it once in a factory in Vietnam, unload it once at a warehouse in Ohio.
segments.tr: ベトナムの工場で一度積み込み、オハイオ州の倉庫で一度降ろすだけです。

segments.src: The two words are often used interchangeably, but there's a useful distinction in contracts.
segments.tr: この2つの言葉はよく同じ意味で使われますが、契約上は有用な違いがあります。

segments.src: *Intermodal* usually describes the physical fact — several modes, one loading unit, often several separate carrier contracts.
segments.tr: *複合一貫輸送（Intermodal）*は通常、物理的な事実を指します。複数の輸送モードを使い、一つの積載単位で運ぶものの、運送会社との契約は複数に分かれることが多いものです。

segments.src: *Multimodal* usually describes the commercial fact — **one contract, one operator liable for the whole door-to-door journey**, typically under a single through bill of lading.
segments.tr: *マルチモーダル輸送（Multimodal）*は通常、商取引上の事実を指します。**1つの契約、戸口から戸口まで全行程に責任を負う1つの運送人**であり、通常は1枚の通し船荷証券の下で行われます。

segments.src: That matters when something goes wrong.
segments.tr: これは何かが起きたときに重要になります。

segments.src: Under separate contracts, you have to prove *which* leg damaged the cargo.
segments.tr: 契約が別々であれば、*どの*区間で貨物が損傷したかを証明しなければなりません。

segments.src: Under a single multimodal contract, you have one party to call.
segments.tr: 1つのマルチモーダル契約であれば、連絡すべき相手は1社だけです。

segments.src: The last mile.** The final leg from a local depot to the customer's door.
segments.tr: ラストマイル。** 地域の集配拠点から顧客の玄関までの最終区間です。

segments.src: It's the leg where economies of scale collapse.
segments.tr: ここでは規模の経済が崩れる区間です。

segments.src: A truck leaving the Port of Long Beach carries one container to one place.
segments.tr: ロングビーチ港を出たトラックは、1つのコンテナを1か所に運びます。

segments.src: A delivery van carries 120 separate packages to 120 separate addresses, each with its own driveway, elevator, gate code, and dog.
segments.tr: 配送バンは、120件の別々の荷物を120か所の別々の住所へ運びます。それぞれに私道、エレベーター、門のコード、そして犬がいます。

segments.src: Industry studies commonly put last-mile delivery at roughly 40–50% of total parcel logistics cost — the shortest leg, the biggest bill.
segments.tr: 業界の調査では、ラストマイル配送は小包物流全体のコストの約40〜50%を占めることが一般的に示されています。最も短い区間なのに、最も大きな請求額になるのです。

segments.src: Two levers dominate last-mile economics:
segments.tr: ラストマイルの経済性を左右する要因は主に2つです。

segments.src: - **Stop density** — how many deliveries you make per mile driven. Dense city blocks are cheap per package; rural routes are brutal.
segments.tr: - **配送密度**: 走行1マイルあたりに何件配送できるか。都市の密集した街区では荷物1個あたりが安く、農村部のルートは過酷です。

segments.src: - **First-attempt success rate** — a failed delivery roughly doubles the cost of that package. This is why lockers, pickup points (PUDO), and "leave at door" photos exist. They're not conveniences; they're cost controls.
segments.tr: - **初回配達成功率**: 配達に失敗すると、その荷物のコストはおおよそ2倍になります。だから宅配ロッカー、受け取りポイント（PUDO）、「玄関に置く」写真確認があるのです。これらは利便性のためではなく、コスト管理のための仕組みです。

segments.src: The Vehicle Routing Problem (VRP).** Once you have 120 packages and 8 vans, someone has to decide who delivers what, in what order.
segments.tr: 配送ルート問題（VRP）。** 荷物が120個、バンが8台あれば、誰がどの荷物を、どの順番で配達するかを決める必要があります。

segments.src: That's the VRP, formally introduced by Dantzig and Ramser in 1959.
segments.tr: これがVRPで、1959年にDantzigとRamserによって正式に提唱されました。

segments.src: Its simpler cousin is the **Traveling Salesman Problem**: one vehicle, visit every stop once, return home, minimize distance.
segments.tr: そのより単純な親戚が**巡回セールスマン問題（TSP）**です。1台の車両が、すべての停留所を一度ずつ訪れて拠点に戻り、距離を最小化します。

segments.src: TSP is just a VRP with a single uncapacitated vehicle.
segments.tr: TSPは、容量制約のない単一車両のVRPにすぎません。

segments.src: Why is this hard?
segments.tr: なぜ難しいのでしょうか。

segments.src: Because the number of possible sequences explodes:
segments.tr: 考えられる順序の数が爆発的に増えるからです:

segments.src: 20 stops  ->  20! orderings  ->  about 2,400,000,000,000,000,000 (2.4 quintillion)
segments.tr: 20 stops  ->  20! orderings  ->  about 2,400,000,000,000,000,000 (2.4 quintillion)

segments.src: Checking them all is hopeless, and VRP is **NP-hard** — no known algorithm finds the guaranteed-best answer quickly as the problem grows.
segments.tr: すべてを調べるのは非現実的であり、VRPは**NP困難**です。問題が大きくなるにつれ、保証された最良解を素早く見つけるアルゴリズムは知られていません。

segments.src: Real routing software doesn't look for the perfect route.
segments.tr: 実際の配車ソフトウェアは完璧なルートを探すわけではありません。

segments.src: It uses **heuristics**: rules that find a very good route fast.
segments.tr: **ヒューリスティクス**、つまり非常に良いルートを素早く見つけるための経験則を使います。

segments.src: The classic is the Clarke–Wright savings algorithm (1964), which asks how much you save by combining two separate out-and-back trips into one:
segments.tr: 代表的なものはClarke–Wright節約法（1964年）で、2つの別々の往復便を1つにまとめると、どれだけ節約できるかを問うものです:

segments.src: savings(i, j) = dist(depot, i) + dist(depot, j) - dist(i, j)
segments.tr: savings(i, j) = dist(depot, i) + dist(depot, j) - dist(i, j)

segments.src: Merge the pairs with the biggest savings first, stop when the truck is full.
segments.tr: 節約量が最も大きい組み合わせから順にまとめ、トラックが満載になったら止めます。

segments.src: Modern solvers layer on constraints that make it realistic: vehicle capacity, driver hours, and **time windows** — "deliver between 2 and 5 p.m."
segments.tr: 現代のソルバーは、現実的にするための制約を加えます。車両の積載量、運転者の労働時間、そして**時間指定枠**です。例えば「午後2時から5時の間に配達」のようなものです。

segments.src: That variant is VRPTW, and every time window you add shrinks the space of legal routes and raises the cost.
segments.tr: この種類はVRPTWと呼ばれ、時間指定枠を1つ追加するごとに、合法なルートの範囲は狭まり、コストは上がります。

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 日常生活の中で

segments.src: You order a $70 pair of running shoes on a Tuesday night.
segments.tr: 火曜日の夜、70ドルのランニングシューズを注文したとします。

segments.src: Here's the actual chain:
segments.tr: 実際の流れは次のとおりです:

segments.src: The shoes were containerized in Vietnam.
segments.tr: このシューズはベトナムでコンテナに積み込まれました。

segments.src: A 40-foot container holds several thousand pairs, so at a few thousand dollars for the ocean leg, the trans-Pacific voyage costs well under **$1 per pair** (figures are illustrative and move constantly with market rates).
segments.tr: 40フィートコンテナには数千足が入るので、海上輸送の費用が数千ドルだとしても、太平洋横断航路の1足あたりのコストは**1ドル未満**に収まります（数字は例示であり、市場運賃によって常に変動します）。

segments.src: The box lands at the Port of Los Angeles/Long Beach.
segments.tr: コンテナはロサンゼルス／ロングビーチ港に到着します。

segments.src: A short-haul **drayage** truck hauls it a few miles to a rail ramp — a leg of maybe 20 miles that can cost a few hundred dollars for the container.
segments.tr: 短距離の**ドレージ（港湾内陸輸送）**トラックが、それを数マイル先の鉄道ラム（積み替え拠点）まで運びます。約20マイルの区間で、コンテナ1本につき数百ドルかかることがあります。

segments.src: Then a BNSF or Union Pacific intermodal train carries it to the Chicago area, the country's biggest inland rail hub, where a truck takes it to a regional distribution center.
segments.tr: その後、BNSFまたはユニオン・パシフィックの複合一貫列車が、国内最大の内陸鉄道ハブであるシカゴ周辺まで運び、そこからトラックが地域の物流センターへ運びます。

segments.src: Everything so far was cheap per pair, because everything so far moved *thousands of pairs at once*.
segments.tr: ここまでのすべては、1足あたりの費用が安くて済みました。なぜなら、ここまでは*何千足もの靴を一度に*動かしていたからです。

segments.src: Then you click "buy."
segments.tr: そして、あなたが「購入」をクリックします。

segments.src: Now one pair, in one box, needs to reach one address.
segments.tr: ここからは、1箱に入った1足を、1つの住所に届けなければなりません。

segments.src: It gets picked, sorted, trucked to a local delivery station, and loaded onto a van with ~120 other packages.
segments.tr: それはピッキングされ、仕分けられ、地域の配送拠点までトラックで運ばれ、約120個の他の荷物と一緒にバンに積み込まれます。

segments.src: That van's driver burns fuel, time, and wages for **your** stop specifically — and the retailer's cost for that final leg is typically several dollars, more than the ocean, rail, and highway legs combined.
segments.tr: そのバンの運転手は、**あなたの**停留所のために燃料、時間、賃金を使います。そして小売業者にとって、この最後の区間の費用は通常数ドルで、海上、鉄道、高速道路の区間を合わせたよりも高くなります。

segments.src: This is also why UPS famously routes its drivers to avoid left turns where practical.
segments.tr: だからこそUPSは、可能な限り左折を避けるようドライバーのルートを組むことで有名です。

segments.src: Waiting to cross oncoming traffic burns fuel and time and raises collision risk.
segments.tr: 対向車線を横切るために待つと、燃料と時間が無駄になり、衝突リスクも高まります。

segments.src: UPS's ORION routing system, rolled out across its U.S.
segments.tr: UPSのORIONルーティングシステムは、米国内の

segments.src: network by 2016, applies that logic at scale; the company has said it saves roughly 100 million miles and about 10 million gallons of fuel a year.
segments.tr: 全ネットワークに2016年までに展開され、その論理を大規模に適用しています。同社によれば、年間で約1億マイル、約1,000万ガロンの燃料を節約しているとのことです。

segments.src: That's a company figure, not an independent audit — but the direction is real.
segments.tr: これは企業側の数字であり、独立した監査によるものではありませんが、その方向性は確かなものです。

segments.src: When you're solving a VRP 55,000 times a day, a small per-stop improvement compounds into a very large number.
segments.tr: 1日55,000回VRPを解くとなると、停留所1件ごとのわずかな改善が、非常に大きな数字に積み上がるのです。

segments.src: ## The 3-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## 3行まとめ

segments.src: 1. Intermodal/multimodal transport makes long-haul freight absurdly cheap by standardizing the box and never touching the goods — and a single multimodal contract means one party is liable end to end.
segments.tr: 1. 複合一貫輸送・マルチモーダル輸送は、箱を標準化し、貨物に一切触れないことで、長距離輸送を驚くほど安くします。また、1つのマルチモーダル契約は、全行程の責任を1社が負うことを意味します。

segments.src: 2. The last mile is the shortest and most expensive leg, roughly 40–50% of parcel cost, and it lives or dies on stop density and first-attempt success.
segments.tr: 2. ラストマイルは最も短く最も高価な区間で、小包費用の約40〜50%を占め、配送密度と初回配達成功率によって成否が決まります。

segments.src: 3. Routing that last mile is the Vehicle Routing Problem — NP-hard, so real systems use heuristics for a very good answer rather than searching forever for a perfect one.
segments.tr: 3. そのラストマイルのルート設計は配送ルート問題（VRP）であり、NP困難なため、実際のシステムは完璧な答えを延々と探すのではなく、ヒューリスティクスで非常に良い答えを求めます。

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ 自己チェッククイズ

segments.src: **Q1.** For a pair of shoes shipped from Asia to a U.S.
segments.tr: **Q1.** アジアから米国の

segments.src: home, which leg typically costs the *most* per unit delivered?
segments.tr: 家庭へ送られた靴について、配送1個あたりで一般的に最も*費用がかかる*のはどの区間ですか。

segments.src: - (A) The trans-Pacific ocean voyage
segments.tr: - (A) 太平洋横断の海上輸送

segments.src: - (B) The intermodal rail move to Chicago
segments.tr: - (B) シカゴまでの複合一貫鉄道輸送

segments.src: - (C) The final van delivery to your door
segments.tr: - (C) お宅の玄関までの最終バン配送

segments.src: - (D) The drayage move out of the port
segments.tr: - (D) 港からのドレージ輸送

segments.src: **Q2.** O/X: The Traveling Salesman Problem can be described as a special case of the Vehicle Routing Problem.
segments.tr: **Q2.** ○/×: 巡回セールスマン問題（TSP）は、配送ルート問題（VRP）の特殊ケースとして説明できる。

segments.src: **Q3.** Which change turns a standard VRP into a "VRPTW"?
segments.tr: **Q3.** 標準的なVRPを「VRPTW」に変えるのはどの変更ですか。

segments.src: - (A) Adding vehicle capacity limits
segments.tr: - (A) 車両の積載量制限を追加する

segments.src: - (B) Adding customer time windows
segments.tr: - (B) 顧客への時間指定枠を追加する

segments.src: - (C) Allowing multiple depots
segments.tr: - (C) 複数の拠点を許可する

segments.src: - (D) Requiring the vehicle to return empty
segments.tr: - (D) 車両が空で戻ることを必須にする

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 今日の用語

de.title: [Logistik 101 #9] Ihre Sneaker überquerten einen Ozean für Kleingeld — dann kosteten die letzten 3 Meilen mehr

segments.src: > Moving freight 8,000 miles is a solved, cheap, standardized problem; moving it the final 3 miles to your porch is the expensive, unsolved one — and the math behind those last 3 miles is genuinely hard.
segments.tr: > Fracht über 8.000 Meilen zu befördern ist ein gelöstes, günstiges, standardisiertes Problem; die letzten 3 Meilen bis zu Ihrer Haustür zu befördern ist dagegen das teure, ungelöste — und die Mathematik dahinter ist wirklich schwierig.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Das heutige Konzept

segments.src: Three ideas do most of the work in modern transportation management.
segments.tr: Drei Ideen leisten in modernem Transportmanagement den größten Teil der Arbeit.

segments.src: Intermodal and multimodal transport.** A shipment rarely uses one mode.
segments.tr: Intermodaler und multimodaler Transport.** Eine Sendung nutzt selten nur ein Verkehrsmittel.

segments.src: It rides a ship, then a truck, then a train, then another truck.
segments.tr: Sie fährt mit einem Schiff, dann einem Lkw, dann einem Zug, dann wieder einem Lkw.

segments.src: The trick that makes this cheap is the **shipping container**: a standardized steel box that gets lifted between modes without anyone touching the goods inside.
segments.tr: Den Trick, der das günstig macht, liefert der **Container**: eine standardisierte Stahlbox, die zwischen den Verkehrsträgern gehoben wird, ohne dass jemand die Ware darin berührt.

segments.src: Load it once in a factory in Vietnam, unload it once at a warehouse in Ohio.
segments.tr: Einmal in einer Fabrik in Vietnam beladen, einmal in einem Lager in Ohio entladen.

segments.src: The two words are often used interchangeably, but there's a useful distinction in contracts.
segments.tr: Die beiden Begriffe werden oft synonym verwendet, aber in Verträgen gibt es eine nützliche Unterscheidung.

segments.src: *Intermodal* usually describes the physical fact — several modes, one loading unit, often several separate carrier contracts.
segments.tr: *Intermodal* beschreibt meist den physischen Sachverhalt — mehrere Verkehrsträger, eine Ladeeinheit, oft mehrere getrennte Frachtverträge.

segments.src: *Multimodal* usually describes the commercial fact — **one contract, one operator liable for the whole door-to-door journey**, typically under a single through bill of lading.
segments.tr: *Multimodal* beschreibt meist den kommerziellen Sachverhalt — **ein Vertrag, ein Betreiber haftet für die gesamte Tür-zu-Tür-Strecke**, typischerweise unter einem durchgehenden Konnossement.

segments.src: That matters when something goes wrong.
segments.tr: Das ist wichtig, wenn etwas schiefgeht.

segments.src: Under separate contracts, you have to prove *which* leg damaged the cargo.
segments.tr: Bei getrennten Verträgen muss man nachweisen, *welcher* Abschnitt die Ware beschädigt hat.

segments.src: Under a single multimodal contract, you have one party to call.
segments.tr: Bei einem einzigen multimodalen Vertrag hat man einen einzigen Ansprechpartner.

segments.src: The last mile.** The final leg from a local depot to the customer's door.
segments.tr: Die letzte Meile.** Der letzte Abschnitt vom lokalen Depot bis zur Haustür des Kunden.

segments.src: It's the leg where economies of scale collapse.
segments.tr: Hier brechen die Skaleneffekte zusammen.

segments.src: A truck leaving the Port of Long Beach carries one container to one place.
segments.tr: Ein Lkw, der den Hafen von Long Beach verlässt, transportiert einen Container an einen Ort.

segments.src: A delivery van carries 120 separate packages to 120 separate addresses, each with its own driveway, elevator, gate code, and dog.
segments.tr: Ein Lieferwagen transportiert 120 einzelne Pakete an 120 einzelne Adressen, jede mit eigener Einfahrt, eigenem Aufzug, eigenem Tor-Code und eigenem Hund.

segments.src: Industry studies commonly put last-mile delivery at roughly 40–50% of total parcel logistics cost — the shortest leg, the biggest bill.
segments.tr: Branchenstudien setzen die Zustellung auf der letzten Meile üblicherweise bei etwa 40–50 % der gesamten Paketlogistikkosten an — der kürzeste Abschnitt, die größte Rechnung.

segments.src: Two levers dominate last-mile economics:
segments.tr: Zwei Hebel bestimmen die Ökonomie der letzten Meile maßgeblich:

segments.src: - **Stop density** — how many deliveries you make per mile driven. Dense city blocks are cheap per package; rural routes are brutal.
segments.tr: - **Haltestellendichte** — wie viele Zustellungen Sie pro gefahrener Meile erreichen. Dichte Stadtblöcke sind pro Paket günstig; ländliche Routen sind brutal.

segments.src: - **First-attempt success rate** — a failed delivery roughly doubles the cost of that package. This is why lockers, pickup points (PUDO), and "leave at door" photos exist. They're not conveniences; they're cost controls.
segments.tr: - **Erstzustellquote** — eine fehlgeschlagene Zustellung verdoppelt etwa die Kosten dieses Pakets. Deshalb gibt es Paketstationen, Abholpunkte (PUDO) und Fotos mit „Ablage an der Tür“. Das sind keine Annehmlichkeiten, sondern Kostenkontrollen.

segments.src: The Vehicle Routing Problem (VRP).** Once you have 120 packages and 8 vans, someone has to decide who delivers what, in what order.
segments.tr: Das Vehicle Routing Problem (VRP).** Sobald Sie 120 Pakete und 8 Lieferwagen haben, muss jemand entscheiden, wer was in welcher Reihenfolge ausliefert.

segments.src: That's the VRP, formally introduced by Dantzig and Ramser in 1959.
segments.tr: Das ist das VRP, formal eingeführt von Dantzig und Ramser im Jahr 1959.

segments.src: Its simpler cousin is the **Traveling Salesman Problem**: one vehicle, visit every stop once, return home, minimize distance.
segments.tr: Sein einfacherer Verwandter ist das **Traveling-Salesman-Problem**: ein Fahrzeug, jeden Halt einmal besuchen, zurückkehren, Distanz minimieren.

segments.src: TSP is just a VRP with a single uncapacitated vehicle.
segments.tr: Das TSP ist im Grunde ein VRP mit einem einzigen, nicht kapazitätsbeschränkten Fahrzeug.

segments.src: Why is this hard?
segments.tr: Warum ist das schwer?

segments.src: Because the number of possible sequences explodes:
segments.tr: Weil die Zahl der möglichen Reihenfolgen explodiert:

segments.src: 20 stops  ->  20! orderings  ->  about 2,400,000,000,000,000,000 (2.4 quintillion)
segments.tr: 20 stops  ->  20! orderings  ->  about 2,400,000,000,000,000,000 (2.4 quintillion)

segments.src: Checking them all is hopeless, and VRP is **NP-hard** — no known algorithm finds the guaranteed-best answer quickly as the problem grows.
segments.tr: Alle durchzuprobieren ist aussichtslos, und das VRP ist **NP-schwer** — kein bekannter Algorithmus findet die garantiert beste Lösung schnell, wenn das Problem wächst.

segments.src: Real routing software doesn't look for the perfect route.
segments.tr: Echte Routing-Software sucht nicht nach der perfekten Route.

segments.src: It uses **heuristics**: rules that find a very good route fast.
segments.tr: Sie verwendet **Heuristiken**: Regeln, die schnell eine sehr gute Route finden.

segments.src: The classic is the Clarke–Wright savings algorithm (1964), which asks how much you save by combining two separate out-and-back trips into one:
segments.tr: Der klassische ist der Clarke-Wright-Savings-Algorithmus (1964), der fragt, wie viel man spart, wenn man zwei getrennte Hin-und-zurück-Fahrten zu einer kombiniert:

segments.src: savings(i, j) = dist(depot, i) + dist(depot, j) - dist(i, j)
segments.tr: savings(i, j) = dist(depot, i) + dist(depot, j) - dist(i, j)

segments.src: Merge the pairs with the biggest savings first, stop when the truck is full.
segments.tr: Die Paare mit den größten Einsparungen zuerst zusammenführen und aufhören, sobald der Lkw voll ist.

segments.src: Modern solvers layer on constraints that make it realistic: vehicle capacity, driver hours, and **time windows** — "deliver between 2 and 5 p.m."
segments.tr: Moderne Solver fügen Nebenbedingungen hinzu, die es realistisch machen: Fahrzeugkapazität, Lenkzeiten und **Zeitfenster** — „Lieferung zwischen 14 und 17 Uhr“.

segments.src: That variant is VRPTW, and every time window you add shrinks the space of legal routes and raises the cost.
segments.tr: Diese Variante heißt VRPTW, und jedes hinzugefügte Zeitfenster verkleinert den Raum zulässiger Routen und erhöht die Kosten.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Im Alltag

segments.src: You order a $70 pair of running shoes on a Tuesday night.
segments.tr: Sie bestellen an einem Dienstagabend ein Paar Laufschuhe für 70 $.

segments.src: Here's the actual chain:
segments.tr: Hier ist die tatsächliche Kette:

segments.src: The shoes were containerized in Vietnam.
segments.tr: Die Schuhe wurden in Vietnam containerisiert.

segments.src: A 40-foot container holds several thousand pairs, so at a few thousand dollars for the ocean leg, the trans-Pacific voyage costs well under **$1 per pair** (figures are illustrative and move constantly with market rates).
segments.tr: Ein 40-Fuß-Container fasst mehrere tausend Paar. Bei einigen tausend Dollar für den Seeweg kostet die Überfahrt über den Pazifik daher deutlich unter **1 $ pro Paar** (Zahlen sind illustrativ und ändern sich mit den Marktpreisen ständig).

segments.src: The box lands at the Port of Los Angeles/Long Beach.
segments.tr: Die Box landet im Hafen von Los Angeles/Long Beach.

segments.src: A short-haul **drayage** truck hauls it a few miles to a rail ramp — a leg of maybe 20 miles that can cost a few hundred dollars for the container.
segments.tr: Ein Nahverkehrs-**Drayage**-Lkw bringt sie einige Meilen zu einer Bahnrampe — ein Abschnitt von etwa 20 Meilen, der für den Container einige hundert Dollar kosten kann.

segments.src: Then a BNSF or Union Pacific intermodal train carries it to the Chicago area, the country's biggest inland rail hub, where a truck takes it to a regional distribution center.
segments.tr: Dann bringt ein intermodaler Zug von BNSF oder Union Pacific sie in den Großraum Chicago, das größte Binnenbahn-Drehkreuz des Landes, wo ein Lkw sie zu einem regionalen Verteilzentrum fährt.

segments.src: Everything so far was cheap per pair, because everything so far moved *thousands of pairs at once*.
segments.tr: Alles bisher war pro Paar günstig, weil alles bisher *tausende Paare auf einmal* bewegt hat.

segments.src: Then you click "buy."
segments.tr: Dann klicken Sie auf „Kaufen“.

segments.src: Now one pair, in one box, needs to reach one address.
segments.tr: Jetzt muss ein einzelnes Paar in einer Box an eine einzelne Adresse gelangen.

segments.src: It gets picked, sorted, trucked to a local delivery station, and loaded onto a van with ~120 other packages.
segments.tr: Es wird kommissioniert, sortiert, zu einer lokalen Zustellstation gefahren und auf einen Lieferwagen mit etwa 120 anderen Paketen geladen.

segments.src: That van's driver burns fuel, time, and wages for **your** stop specifically — and the retailer's cost for that final leg is typically several dollars, more than the ocean, rail, and highway legs combined.
segments.tr: Der Fahrer dieses Lieferwagens verbraucht Treibstoff, Zeit und Lohn speziell für **Ihren** Halt — und die Kosten des Händlers für diesen letzten Abschnitt liegen typischerweise bei mehreren Dollar, mehr als die Abschnitte Seeweg, Schiene und Autobahn zusammen.

segments.src: This is also why UPS famously routes its drivers to avoid left turns where practical.
segments.tr: Deshalb lässt UPS seine Fahrer bekanntlich, wo es praktikabel ist, Linksabbiegen vermeiden.

segments.src: Waiting to cross oncoming traffic burns fuel and time and raises collision risk.
segments.tr: Das Warten, um den Gegenverkehr zu queren, verbraucht Treibstoff und Zeit und erhöht das Unfallrisiko.

segments.src: UPS's ORION routing system, rolled out across its U.S.
segments.tr: Das Routing-System ORION von UPS, das in seinem US-

segments.src: network by 2016, applies that logic at scale; the company has said it saves roughly 100 million miles and about 10 million gallons of fuel a year.
segments.tr: Netz bis 2016 eingeführt wurde, wendet diese Logik im großen Maßstab an; das Unternehmen gibt an, dass es jährlich rund 100 Millionen Meilen und etwa 10 Millionen Gallonen Treibstoff einspart.

segments.src: That's a company figure, not an independent audit — but the direction is real.
segments.tr: Das ist eine Angabe des Unternehmens, kein unabhängiges Audit — aber die Richtung stimmt.

segments.src: When you're solving a VRP 55,000 times a day, a small per-stop improvement compounds into a very large number.
segments.tr: Wenn man ein VRP 55.000-mal am Tag löst, summiert sich eine kleine Verbesserung pro Halt zu einer sehr großen Zahl.

segments.src: ## The 3-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## Die Zusammenfassung in 3 Zeilen

segments.src: 1. Intermodal/multimodal transport makes long-haul freight absurdly cheap by standardizing the box and never touching the goods — and a single multimodal contract means one party is liable end to end.
segments.tr: 1. Intermodaler/multimodaler Transport macht den Fernfrachtverkehr dank standardisierter Box und unberührter Ware absurd günstig — und ein einziger multimodaler Vertrag bedeutet, dass eine Partei durchgehend haftet.

segments.src: 2. The last mile is the shortest and most expensive leg, roughly 40–50% of parcel cost, and it lives or dies on stop density and first-attempt success.
segments.tr: 2. Die letzte Meile ist der kürzeste und teuerste Abschnitt, etwa 40–50 % der Paketkosten, und sie steht und fällt mit der Haltestellendichte und der Erstzustellquote.

segments.src: 3. Routing that last mile is the Vehicle Routing Problem — NP-hard, so real systems use heuristics for a very good answer rather than searching forever for a perfect one.
segments.tr: 3. Die Routenplanung der letzten Meile ist das Vehicle Routing Problem — NP-schwer, daher verwenden reale Systeme Heuristiken für eine sehr gute Lösung, statt ewig nach einer perfekten zu suchen.

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Begriffe des Tages

segments.src: - **Intermodal transport** — Moving goods by two or more modes in the same loading unit (usually a container), without handling the goods themselves at transfer points.
segments.tr: - **Intermodaler Transport** — Der Transport von Waren mit zwei oder mehr Verkehrsträgern in derselben Ladeeinheit (meist einem Container), ohne dass die Ware an den Übergabepunkten selbst umgeschlagen wird.

segments.src: - **Multimodal transport** — The commercial version: one contract and one operator responsible for the entire door-to-door journey, typically under a through bill of lading.
segments.tr: - **Multimodaler Transport** — Die kommerzielle Variante: ein Vertrag und ein Betreiber, der für die gesamte Tür-zu-Tür-Strecke verantwortlich ist, typischerweise unter einem durchgehenden Konnossement.

segments.src: - **Drayage** — Short-distance trucking of a container, usually between a port, rail ramp, or nearby warehouse.
segments.tr: - **Drayage** — Kurzstrecken-Lkw-Transport eines Containers, meist zwischen Hafen, Bahnrampe oder nahegelegenem Lager.

segments.src: - **Stop density** — Deliveries made per mile driven; the single biggest driver of last-mile cost per package.
segments.tr: - **Haltestellendichte** — Zustellungen pro gefahrener Meile; der mit Abstand wichtigste Treiber der Kosten pro Paket auf der letzten Meile.

segments.src: - **Vehicle Routing Problem (VRP)** — Deciding which vehicle serves which stops in what order to minimize cost under constraints; NP-hard, so solved in practice with heuristics.
segments.tr: - **Vehicle Routing Problem (VRP)** — Festlegen, welches Fahrzeug welche Halte in welcher Reihenfolge bedient, um die Kosten unter Nebenbedingungen zu minimieren; NP-schwer, daher in der Praxis mit Heuristiken gelöst.

segments.src: - **Time window** — A promised delivery interval (e.g., 2–5 p.m.); each one added constrains the route and raises cost.
segments.tr: - **Zeitfenster** — Ein zugesagtes Lieferintervall (z. B. 14–17 Uhr); jedes zusätzliche Zeitfenster schränkt die Route ein und erhöht die Kosten.

segments.src: *Answers: **Q1 — (C).** The last mile is the shortest leg but carries the least scale, commonly 40–50% of total parcel logistics cost.
segments.tr: *Antworten: **F1 — (C).** Die letzte Meile ist der kürzeste Abschnitt, hat aber die geringste Skalierung und macht typischerweise 40–50 % der gesamten Paketlogistikkosten aus.

segments.src: **Q2 — O (True).** A VRP with a single vehicle, no capacity limit, and one depot reduces exactly to the TSP.
segments.tr: **F2 — O (Richtig).** Ein VRP mit einem einzigen Fahrzeug, ohne Kapazitätsgrenze und mit einem Depot reduziert sich genau auf das TSP.

segments.src: **Q3 — (B).** Time windows define the VRPTW variant; capacity limits are already part of the standard capacitated VRP.*
segments.tr: **F3 — (B).** Zeitfenster definieren die Variante VRPTW; Kapazitätsgrenzen sind bereits Bestandteil des Standard-VRP mit Kapazitätsbeschränkung.*

vi.title: [Logistics 101 #9] Đôi giày thể thao của bạn vượt đại dương với giá rẻ — rồi chặng 3 dặm cuối lại đắt hơn

segments.src: > Moving freight 8,000 miles is a solved, cheap, standardized problem; moving it the final 3 miles to your porch is the expensive, unsolved one — and the math behind those last 3 miles is genuinely hard.
segments.tr: > Vận chuyển hàng hóa 8,000 dặm là một bài toán đã được giải quyết, rẻ và được chuẩn hóa; còn đưa hàng đi chặng 3 dặm cuối cùng đến tận hiên nhà bạn mới là phần tốn kém và chưa được giải quyết — và phép tính đằng sau 3 dặm cuối đó thực sự khó.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Khái niệm hôm nay

segments.src: Three ideas do most of the work in modern transportation management.
segments.tr: Ba ý tưởng đảm nhận phần lớn công việc trong quản lý vận tải hiện đại.

segments.src: Intermodal and multimodal transport.** A shipment rarely uses one mode.
segments.tr: Vận tải liên phương thức và đa phương thức.** Một lô hàng hiếm khi chỉ dùng một phương thức.

segments.src: It rides a ship, then a truck, then a train, then another truck.
segments.tr: Nó đi bằng tàu, rồi xe tải, rồi tàu hỏa, rồi lại xe tải khác.

segments.src: The trick that makes this cheap is the **shipping container**: a standardized steel box that gets lifted between modes without anyone touching the goods inside.
segments.tr: Thứ làm cho việc này rẻ là **container vận chuyển**: một hộp thép tiêu chuẩn được nâng từ phương thức này sang phương thức khác mà không ai chạm vào hàng hóa bên trong.

segments.src: Load it once in a factory in Vietnam, unload it once at a warehouse in Ohio.
segments.tr: Chất hàng một lần tại nhà máy ở Việt Nam, dỡ một lần tại kho ở Ohio.

segments.src: The two words are often used interchangeably, but there's a useful distinction in contracts.
segments.tr: Hai thuật ngữ này thường được dùng thay thế cho nhau, nhưng trong hợp đồng có một sự khác biệt hữu ích.

segments.src: *Intermodal* usually describes the physical fact — several modes, one loading unit, often several separate carrier contracts.
segments.tr: *Intermodal* thường mô tả thực tế vật lý — nhiều phương thức, một đơn vị chất hàng, thường có nhiều hợp đồng vận chuyển riêng biệt.

segments.src: *Multimodal* usually describes the commercial fact — **one contract, one operator liable for the whole door-to-door journey**, typically under a single through bill of lading.
segments.tr: *Multimodal* thường mô tả thực tế thương mại — **một hợp đồng, một đơn vị vận hành chịu trách nhiệm cho toàn bộ hành trình từ cửa đến cửa**, thường theo một vận đơn suốt tuyến duy nhất.

segments.src: That matters when something goes wrong.
segments.tr: Điều đó quan trọng khi có sự cố.

segments.src: Under separate contracts, you have to prove *which* leg damaged the cargo.
segments.tr: Với các hợp đồng riêng lẻ, bạn phải chứng minh *chặng nào* đã làm hỏng hàng hóa.

segments.src: Under a single multimodal contract, you have one party to call.
segments.tr: Với một hợp đồng đa phương thức duy nhất, bạn chỉ cần liên hệ một bên.

segments.src: The last mile.** The final leg from a local depot to the customer's door.
segments.tr: Chặng cuối (last mile).** Chặng cuối cùng từ kho trung chuyển địa phương đến cửa nhà khách hàng.

segments.src: It's the leg where economies of scale collapse.
segments.tr: Đây là chặng mà lợi thế quy mô sụp đổ.

segments.src: A truck leaving the Port of Long Beach carries one container to one place.
segments.tr: Một xe tải rời Cảng Long Beach chở một container đến một địa điểm.

segments.src: A delivery van carries 120 separate packages to 120 separate addresses, each with its own driveway, elevator, gate code, and dog.
segments.tr: Một xe giao hàng chở 120 kiện hàng riêng biệt đến 120 địa chỉ riêng biệt, mỗi nơi có lối vào, thang máy, mã cổng và con chó riêng.

segments.src: Industry studies commonly put last-mile delivery at roughly 40–50% of total parcel logistics cost — the shortest leg, the biggest bill.
segments.tr: Các nghiên cứu ngành thường ước tính chi phí giao hàng chặng cuối chiếm khoảng 40–50% tổng chi phí logistics bưu kiện — chặng ngắn nhất, nhưng hóa đơn lớn nhất.

segments.src: Two levers dominate last-mile economics:
segments.tr: Hai đòn bẩy chi phối kinh tế của chặng cuối:

segments.src: - **Stop density** — how many deliveries you make per mile driven. Dense city blocks are cheap per package; rural routes are brutal.
segments.tr: - **Mật độ điểm giao (stop density)** — số lần giao hàng trên mỗi dặm di chuyển. Các khu phố dày đặc ở thành phố thì rẻ tính trên mỗi kiện; tuyến nông thôn thì rất tốn kém.

segments.src: - **First-attempt success rate** — a failed delivery roughly doubles the cost of that package. This is why lockers, pickup points (PUDO), and "leave at door" photos exist. They're not conveniences; they're cost controls.
segments.tr: - **Tỷ lệ giao thành công ngay lần đầu** — một lần giao thất bại làm gần như tăng gấp đôi chi phí của kiện hàng đó. Đây là lý do tồn tại tủ nhận hàng, điểm nhận hàng (PUDO) và ảnh "để trước cửa". Chúng không phải tiện ích; chúng là công cụ kiểm soát chi phí.

segments.src: The Vehicle Routing Problem (VRP).** Once you have 120 packages and 8 vans, someone has to decide who delivers what, in what order.
segments.tr: Bài toán định tuyến phương tiện (VRP).** Khi có 120 kiện hàng và 8 xe giao hàng, phải có người quyết định xe nào giao gì, theo thứ tự nào.

segments.src: That's the VRP, formally introduced by Dantzig and Ramser in 1959.
segments.tr: Đó là VRP, được Dantzig và Ramser giới thiệu chính thức năm 1959.

segments.src: Its simpler cousin is the **Traveling Salesman Problem**: one vehicle, visit every stop once, return home, minimize distance.
segments.tr: Người anh em đơn giản hơn của nó là **bài toán người bán hàng du lịch (TSP)**: một phương tiện, ghé thăm mọi điểm đúng một lần, quay về xuất phát và giảm thiểu quãng đường.

segments.src: TSP is just a VRP with a single uncapacitated vehicle.
segments.tr: TSP chỉ là một VRP với một phương tiện duy nhất và không giới hạn tải trọng.

segments.src: Why is this hard?
segments.tr: Vì sao bài toán này khó?

segments.src: Because the number of possible sequences explodes:
segments.tr: Vì số thứ tự có thể có bùng nổ:

segments.src: 20 stops  ->  20! orderings  ->  about 2,400,000,000,000,000,000 (2.4 quintillion)
segments.tr: 20 stops  ->  20! orderings  ->  about 2,400,000,000,000,000,000 (2.4 quintillion)

segments.src: Checking them all is hopeless, and VRP is **NP-hard** — no known algorithm finds the guaranteed-best answer quickly as the problem grows.
segments.tr: Kiểm tra tất cả là vô vọng, và VRP là **NP-khó** — chưa có thuật toán nào đã biết tìm được lời giải tốt nhất được đảm bảo một cách nhanh chóng khi bài toán lớn dần.

segments.src: Real routing software doesn't look for the perfect route.
segments.tr: Phần mềm định tuyến thực tế không tìm tuyến đường hoàn hảo.

segments.src: It uses **heuristics**: rules that find a very good route fast.
segments.tr: Nó dùng **heuristic**: các quy tắc tìm ra tuyến đường rất tốt một cách nhanh chóng.

segments.src: The classic is the Clarke–Wright savings algorithm (1964), which asks how much you save by combining two separate out-and-back trips into one:
segments.tr: Thuật toán tiết kiệm Clarke–Wright (1964) là ví dụ kinh điển, nó hỏi bạn tiết kiệm được bao nhiêu khi gộp hai chuyến đi-và-về riêng biệt thành một:

segments.src: savings(i, j) = dist(depot, i) + dist(depot, j) - dist(i, j)
segments.tr: savings(i, j) = dist(depot, i) + dist(depot, j) - dist(i, j)

segments.src: Merge the pairs with the biggest savings first, stop when the truck is full.
segments.tr: Gộp các cặp có mức tiết kiệm lớn nhất trước, dừng lại khi xe đã đầy.

segments.src: Modern solvers layer on constraints that make it realistic: vehicle capacity, driver hours, and **time windows** — "deliver between 2 and 5 p.m."
segments.tr: Các bộ giải hiện đại bổ sung thêm ràng buộc để bài toán sát thực tế: sức chứa xe, giờ làm việc của tài xế, và **khung thời gian giao hàng** — "giao từ 2 đến 5 giờ chiều".

segments.src: That variant is VRPTW, and every time window you add shrinks the space of legal routes and raises the cost.
segments.tr: Biến thể đó là VRPTW, và mỗi khung thời gian bạn thêm vào làm thu hẹp không gian các tuyến hợp lệ và làm tăng chi phí.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Trong đời sống hằng ngày

segments.src: You order a $70 pair of running shoes on a Tuesday night.
segments.tr: Bạn đặt một đôi giày chạy bộ giá 70 USD vào tối thứ Ba.

segments.src: Here's the actual chain:
segments.tr: Đây là chuỗi diễn ra thực tế:

segments.src: The shoes were containerized in Vietnam.
segments.tr: Đôi giày được đóng vào container ở Việt Nam.

segments.src: A 40-foot container holds several thousand pairs, so at a few thousand dollars for the ocean leg, the trans-Pacific voyage costs well under **$1 per pair** (figures are illustrative and move constantly with market rates).
segments.tr: Một container 40 feet chứa vài nghìn đôi, nên với vài nghìn đô la cho chặng đường biển, hành trình xuyên Thái Bình Dương tốn dưới **1 USD mỗi đôi** (số liệu chỉ mang tính minh họa và thay đổi liên tục theo giá thị trường).

segments.src: The box lands at the Port of Los Angeles/Long Beach.
segments.tr: Container cập Cảng Los Angeles/Long Beach.

segments.src: A short-haul **drayage** truck hauls it a few miles to a rail ramp — a leg of maybe 20 miles that can cost a few hundred dollars for the container.
segments.tr: Một xe tải **drayage** cự ly ngắn chở nó vài dặm đến bãi đường sắt — chặng khoảng 20 dặm có thể tốn vài trăm đô la cho container.

segments.src: Then a BNSF or Union Pacific intermodal train carries it to the Chicago area, the country's biggest inland rail hub, where a truck takes it to a regional distribution center.
segments.tr: Sau đó, tàu hỏa liên phương thức của BNSF hoặc Union Pacific chở nó đến khu vực Chicago, trung tâm đường sắt nội địa lớn nhất của đất nước, nơi một xe tải đưa nó đến trung tâm phân phối khu vực.

segments.src: Everything so far was cheap per pair, because everything so far moved *thousands of pairs at once*.
segments.tr: Mọi thứ cho đến nay đều rẻ tính trên mỗi đôi, vì mọi thứ cho đến nay đều vận chuyển *hàng nghìn đôi cùng lúc*.

segments.src: Then you click "buy."
segments.tr: Rồi bạn nhấn "mua".

segments.src: Now one pair, in one box, needs to reach one address.
segments.tr: Giờ đây một đôi, trong một hộp, cần đến một địa chỉ.

segments.src: It gets picked, sorted, trucked to a local delivery station, and loaded onto a van with ~120 other packages.
segments.tr: Nó được lấy hàng, phân loại, chở bằng xe tải đến trạm giao hàng địa phương, và xếp lên một xe giao hàng cùng khoảng 120 kiện khác.

segments.src: That van's driver burns fuel, time, and wages for **your** stop specifically — and the retailer's cost for that final leg is typically several dollars, more than the ocean, rail, and highway legs combined.
segments.tr: Tài xế của chiếc xe đó tốn nhiên liệu, thời gian và tiền công cho **điểm giao của bạn** — và chi phí của nhà bán lẻ cho chặng cuối cùng này thường là vài đô la, nhiều hơn tổng chi phí của các chặng tàu biển, tàu hỏa và đường cao tốc cộng lại.

segments.src: This is also why UPS famously routes its drivers to avoid left turns where practical.
segments.tr: Đây cũng là lý do UPS nổi tiếng với việc định tuyến tài xế tránh rẽ trái khi có thể.

segments.src: Waiting to cross oncoming traffic burns fuel and time and raises collision risk.
segments.tr: Chờ để cắt dòng xe đi ngược chiều tốn nhiên liệu và thời gian, đồng thời làm tăng nguy cơ va chạm.

segments.src: UPS's ORION routing system, rolled out across its U.S.
segments.tr: Hệ thống định tuyến ORION của UPS, được triển khai trên toàn mạng lưới tại Hoa Kỳ

segments.src: network by 2016, applies that logic at scale; the company has said it saves roughly 100 million miles and about 10 million gallons of fuel a year.
segments.tr: vào năm 2016, áp dụng logic đó ở quy mô lớn; công ty cho biết nó tiết kiệm khoảng 100 triệu dặm và khoảng 10 triệu gallon nhiên liệu mỗi năm.

segments.src: That's a company figure, not an independent audit — but the direction is real.
segments.tr: Đó là con số của công ty, không phải kiểm toán độc lập — nhưng xu hướng là có thật.

segments.src: When you're solving a VRP 55,000 times a day, a small per-stop improvement compounds into a very large number.
segments.tr: Khi bạn giải bài toán VRP 55.000 lần mỗi ngày, một cải thiện nhỏ ở mỗi điểm dừng sẽ cộng dồn thành một con số rất lớn.

segments.src: ## The 3-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## Tóm tắt 3 dòng

segments.src: 1. Intermodal/multimodal transport makes long-haul freight absurdly cheap by standardizing the box and never touching the goods — and a single multimodal contract means one party is liable end to end.
segments.tr: 1. Vận tải liên phương thức/đa phương thức làm cho vận tải đường dài rẻ một cách phi lý bằng cách chuẩn hóa hộp chứa và không bao giờ chạm vào hàng hóa — và một hợp đồng đa phương thức duy nhất nghĩa là một bên chịu trách nhiệm từ đầu đến cuối.

segments.src: 2. The last mile is the shortest and most expensive leg, roughly 40–50% of parcel cost, and it lives or dies on stop density and first-attempt success.
segments.tr: 2. Chặng cuối là chặng ngắn nhất và tốn kém nhất, chiếm khoảng 40–50% chi phí bưu kiện, và phụ thuộc hoàn toàn vào mật độ điểm giao và tỷ lệ giao thành công ngay lần đầu.

segments.src: 3. Routing that last mile is the Vehicle Routing Problem — NP-hard, so real systems use heuristics for a very good answer rather than searching forever for a perfect one.
segments.tr: 3. Định tuyến chặng cuối chính là Bài toán định tuyến phương tiện (VRP) — NP-khó, nên các hệ thống thực tế dùng heuristic để có lời giải rất tốt thay vì tìm mãi một lời giải hoàn hảo.

segments.tr: **Q3.** Thay đổi nào biến một VRP tiêu chuẩn thành "VRPTW"?

segments.tr: - (A) Thêm giới hạn sức chứa của phương tiện

segments.tr: - (D) Yêu cầu phương tiện phải quay về không tải

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Thuật ngữ hôm nay

segments.src: - **Intermodal transport** — Moving goods by two or more modes in the same loading unit (usually a container), without handling the goods themselves at transfer points.
segments.tr: - **Vận tải liên phương thức (Intermodal transport)** — Vận chuyển hàng hóa bằng hai hoặc nhiều phương thức trong cùng một đơn vị chất hàng (thường là container), mà không xử lý hàng hóa tại các điểm chuyển tiếp.

segments.src: - **Multimodal transport** — The commercial version: one contract and one operator responsible for the entire door-to-door journey, typically under a through bill of lading.
segments.tr: - **Vận tải đa phương thức (Multimodal transport)** — Phiên bản thương mại: một hợp đồng và một đơn vị vận hành chịu trách nhiệm cho toàn bộ hành trình từ cửa đến cửa, thường theo vận đơn suốt tuyến.

segments.src: - **Drayage** — Short-distance trucking of a container, usually between a port, rail ramp, or nearby warehouse.
segments.tr: - **Drayage** — Vận chuyển container bằng xe tải cự ly ngắn, thường giữa cảng, bãi đường sắt hoặc kho gần đó.

segments.src: - **Stop density** — Deliveries made per mile driven; the single biggest driver of last-mile cost per package.
segments.tr: - **Mật độ điểm giao (Stop density)** — Số lần giao hàng trên mỗi dặm di chuyển; là yếu tố lớn nhất quyết định chi phí chặng cuối trên mỗi kiện.

segments.src: - **Vehicle Routing Problem (VRP)** — Deciding which vehicle serves which stops in what order to minimize cost under constraints; NP-hard, so solved in practice with heuristics.
segments.tr: - **Bài toán định tuyến phương tiện (Vehicle Routing Problem, VRP)** — Quyết định phương tiện nào phục vụ những điểm dừng nào, theo thứ tự nào, để giảm thiểu chi phí dưới các ràng buộc; là bài toán NP-khó, nên trên thực tế được giải bằng heuristic.

segments.src: - **Time window** — A promised delivery interval (e.g., 2–5 p.m.); each one added constrains the route and raises cost.
segments.tr: - **Khung thời gian giao hàng (Time window)** — Khoảng thời gian giao hàng đã hứa (ví dụ 2–5 giờ chiều); mỗi khung thêm vào sẽ ràng buộc tuyến đường và làm tăng chi phí.

segments.src: *Answers: **Q1 — (C).** The last mile is the shortest leg but carries the least scale, commonly 40–50% of total parcel logistics cost.
segments.tr: *Đáp án: **Q1 — (C).** Chặng cuối là chặng ngắn nhất nhưng có quy mô thấp nhất, thường chiếm 40–50% tổng chi phí logistics bưu kiện.

segments.src: **Q2 — O (True).** A VRP with a single vehicle, no capacity limit, and one depot reduces exactly to the TSP.
segments.tr: **Q2 — O (Đúng).** VRP với một phương tiện duy nhất, không giới hạn sức chứa và một kho trung tâm sẽ quy về đúng TSP.

segments.src: **Q3 — (B).** Time windows define the VRPTW variant; capacity limits are already part of the standard capacitated VRP.*
segments.tr: **Q3 — (B).** Khung thời gian định nghĩa biến thể VRPTW; giới hạn sức chứa vốn đã là một phần của VRP có sức chứa tiêu chuẩn.*
